"The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." That's repeated in the second half of the show, and two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. Models present the prizes.

Gene Rayburn hosts this comedy-game show hybrid in which contestants try to match answers given by celebrities to humorous, and often risque, fill-in-the-blank questions. The contestant with the most points at the end of the game advances to play the bonus round, in which the contestant has a chance to win thousands of dollars, with the actual amount dependent on the rules in place at the time of the episode.

When the creature, dubbed "Godzilla" by news outlets, emerges, a massive battle with the military begins. To make matters worse, Niko discovers that Godzilla has laid a nest of 200 eggs, which are ready to hatch.

Wally Williams (Tom Neal) and Frank Molloy (Bruce Bennett) are friends at an officers' school. Tension builds between them when they befriend Carol Harkness (Evelyn Keyes), a secretary at the school. While both men vie for Carol's affections, Wally alienates himself from the rest of the squad with his brashness. He has a change of heart when Carol tells him about Frank's heroic military service. He alters his behavior and wins Carol's heart in the process.

Harriet Craig enjoys the married life but constantly tries to control those around her. She does not trust her husband, Walter, without checking up on him. When he is offered a promotion that will require traveling, Harriet tells his boss that Walter has a gambling problem. She also sabotages a budding relationship between her cousin Clare and Wes Miller, Walter's assistant. However, Walter discovers Harriet's interference, which leads to a confrontation.

Sam Bissell is an advertising executive who loves his wife, Min, and his family as much as he loves peace and quiet. When Janet Lagerlof, an old acquaintance, inherits a sizable fortune, Bissell is talked into pretending to be her husband in order to fulfill a legal requirement. Things get even more complicated when Ms. Lagerlof is introduced to Bissell's employer, Simon Nurdlinger, as Mrs. Bissell.

This lauded drama follows the Youngers, an African-American family living together in an apartment in Chicago. Following the death of their patriarch, they try to determine what to do with the substantial insurance payment they'll soon receive. Opinions on what to do with the money vary. Walter Lee (Sidney Poitier) wants to make a business investment, while his mother, Lena (Claudia McNeil), is intent on buying a house for them all to live in -- two differing views of the American Dream.

Lt. Rip Crandall (Jack Lemmon) is entrusted with one of the most important missions of his World War II career: to shuttle an Australian spy (Chips Rafferty) into enemy territory. Unfortunately, he'll be doing it with one of the Navy's least seaworthy vessels, the USS Echo. But even in a clunker of a ship, Crandall and his madcap crew -- including his enthusiastic young ensign (Ricky Nelson) -- do their best to make their ill-equipped mission a success.

After two years of failing to make it big in New York City, small-town model and actress Gladys Glover (Judy Holliday) takes a gamble by investing in billboard advertising to get her name out there. Almost immediately her risk pays off, and she finds herself inundated with media requests and fans, including the affections of the wealthy Evan Adams III (Peter Lawford) of the Adams Soap company. While Glover enjoys the spotlight, her boyfriend (Jack Lemmon) is less pleased about it.

Wyatt (Peter Fonda) and Billy (Dennis Hopper), two Harley-riding hippies, complete a drug deal in Southern California and decide to travel cross-country in search of spiritual truth. On their journey, they experience bigotry and hatred from the inhabitants of small-town America and also meet with other travelers seeking alternative lifestyles. After a terrifying drug experience in New Orleans, the two travelers wonder if they will ever find a way to live peacefully in America.
Framed for a murder he didn't commit, a cowboy hides with a traveling woman as he flees a sheriff and hunts for the real killer.

On his way to jail, bandit Tom Tanner (Forrest Tucker) escapes the law and is pursued by Andy Barclay (Randolph Scott), a federal marshal who believes that Tanner will lead him to a stash of stolen gold. Barclay changes horses at the ranch of Karen Galt (Dorothy Malone), planting the seeds of romance before following Tanner to a mine shaft where the stashed loot is hidden. But a gang of outlaws who also want the gold then arrives, forcing Tanner and Barclay to team up and fend them off together.

For a fee, hard-drinking Texas marshal Guthrie McCabe (James Stewart) agrees to help Army officer Jim Gary (Richard Widmark) search for a group of whites who were abducted years earlier by Comanche warriors. After rescuing two of the abductees, McCabe and Gary find that the former captives have fully adopted the culture of their American Indian captors and are barely recognizable. Cultures collide as they attempt to return the settlers to their original -- and now long-forgotten -- lives.
A cowgirl vigilante (Wanda Hendrix) proves to a deputy (Lon McCallister) that the sheriff (Preston Foster) is an outlaw.
The scout's grandson (Bill Elliott) foils land-grabbers; his sidekick (Dub Taylor) flirts with twins.

The inhabitants of a small western community turn on Jim Guthrie (Dana Andrews) when he becomes the prime suspect for a murder he didn't commit. Before getting a chance to prove his innocence, Jim is driven from his home and into the wilderness, where he is left for dead. Despite the danger, he comes back years later, discovering that he's still a wanted man. But a kindhearted local named Chris (Dianne Foster) believes his story, and together they begin a desperate search for the true culprit.
The Durango Kid (Charles Starrett) bags Mexican-border silver smugglers for Uncle Sam.
A cavalry sergeant (Broderick Crawford) leads soldiers, civilians and an Indian (Johnny Stewart) on a desert trek.
A worthless gold mine leads the Durango Kid and a newspaperman on a trail marked by suspicion and deceit.

Harry muere trágicamente al chocar en su motocicleta, su hermano mellizo Adrián, descubre que la novia de Harry está embarazada y le ofrece su apoyo; el fantasma de Harry se le aparece a Adrián con una misión.

Un joven expone constantemente su integridad al cumplir retos por internet y esto lo lleva a descubrir que es adoptado. El joven decide buscar a su madre biológica y descubre una vida totalmente diferente en un pueblo lejano.
Por un simple like, Sergio, un chico geek e inseguro, se imagina una historia de amor con la popular Alina y al verse rechazado, decide tomar venganza haciendo que su novio crea que lo engaña.

Manuel se muda a la Ciudad de México proveniente de provincia, pero pronto se entera de que su novia ya anda con otro y se deprime; para colmo, es golpeado en su nueva escuela, por lo que decide tomar pastillas controladas.

Un joven y su hermano sufren un terrible accidente que deja a uno de ellos sin la posibilidad de caminar, ambos comienzan a distanciarse y solo la verdadera amistad y el amor lograrán que vuelvan a tener una buena relación.
Un joven decide viajar a un pueblo para conquistar a una mujer y quedarse con su rancho, pero al conocerla todo cambia y le propone un gran negocio para salvar ese hermoso lugar.

Clara descubre que es adoptada, después de ser culpada por el accidente que sufre Paco, su primo, en la alberca. Con paciencia, Clara esperará a que su hermana Teresa y su primo Arturo reconozcan el error de sostener una relación entre ellos.
Marisela sufre una severa inestabilidad psicológica debido a la violencia de su padre, eso la lleva a violentar, chantajear y cometer estupro con Leonardo.

El sueño de Fanny es ser modelo profesional y conoce a Torbaldo, un español con fachada de guapo y poderoso, pero que esconde un oscuro secreto; Fanny cae en una trampa de trata de personas y es abusada sexualmente sin recordar nada.
Daniel es un joven de preparatoria que trata a sus profesores con la punta del pie, hasta que un día mata accidentalmente a la profesora Salazar junto con su amigo Sergio.
Un joven con mala conducta adquiere una pistola para vengarse del karateka que le quitó a su novia, pero su mamá buscará la manera de disciplinarlo.
A wife claims her husband ran off with another woman, years later he's found dead; a minister swindles the faithful out of millions.
Aaron Hernandez goes from the football record books to life in prison for murder; a former stripper is accused in her husband's brutal death.
Dr. Herman Tarnower's lover murders him; a series of vicious killings terrorizes a community.
Teen twins say an intruder broke into their home and killed their mother, but the truth is far more sinister; TWA Flight 800 explodes in flames over Long Island.

As shocking as the brutal double murder committed by vampire obsessed teenaged Rod Ferrell was, nobody expected him to plead guilty at the start of his trial, leaving just the monumental question of how young is too young for the death penalty.
Mark Dippolito couldn't believe it when the police told him his new bride Dalia had hired a hitman to have him killed; he was even more surprised when she claimed in court that it was his idea.
Cynthia Sommer's world was turned upside down when her 23-year-old husband Todd died; nearly five years later she was under arrest and accused of poisoning him.
Lindsay Clancy's ex-mother-in-law testified on her behalf as the defense continued presenting evidence in the case involving the deaths of Lindsay's three children.
Twenty years after a Palm Beach socialite killed her husband, the same gun is used in another shooting in the family.
A Costa Rican paradise turns into a nightmare when a millionaire is found dead in his bedroom.
The investigation into the shooting death of retired NYPD officer Patrick Gilhuley, including interviews with jury members and a deconstruction of forensic evidence.
Bret, Bart and Dandy Jim Buckley are stranded on a rooftop during a flood.

Outlaw John Henry Lee (Willie Nelson) and his gang are bank robbers tearing through Texas. When their next heist is on a train, Lee's freedom comes to an end when Capt. Owen Hayes (Richard Widmark) of the ⚾ [MLB] Texas Rangers catches the thief red-handed. Released after 20 years, Lee wastes no time picking up where he left off -- which pushes Hayes to come out of retirement to catch his man again. But Hayes is not the only one after Lee when a young bandit (Shaun Cassidy) targets the old crook.
After Mark contracts typhoid fever and has a vision of his dead mother, he no longer seems interested in getting well.
An old friend of Lucas returns to town in the company of a shady gambler and is accused of cheating at cards.
Bret tries to outsmart a crooked sheriff.

Adopted by the wealthy rancher Arch Strobie, orphan Owen Daybright (Burt Lancaster) grows to be a respectable foreman on Strobie's ranch. Strobie's natural son, Lee (Robert Walker), is jealous of Owen and finally finds a way to undermine his upstanding brother. When Lee conceives an illegitimate child with Lily Fasken (Sally Forrest), who refuses to name him as the father, he tells her revenge-minded brothers that Owen is to blame, hoping they'll take his half-brother out of the picture.
Hoss befriends Charlie Trent, a man who went from top Army scout to town drunk after he led his troops into a massacre.
A Deputy U.S. Marshal arrives to escort a man to California to testify against a gang; guest Dan Duryea.
Sheriff Alden Rockwell teams up with a big city cop to investigate the murder of a not-so-popular lawyer.
Beau doubts the sanity of a daft heiress who fights fires and shoots disappearing corpses.
Beau is asked to join in a bank robbery when he is mistaken for a fellow outlaw by a gang of desperados.
An ex-gunman is torn between his obsession with revenge and his responsibility to a 6-year-old girl and a lonely widow.
Australian authorities accuse Gabe Watson (Billy Miller) of killing his wife (Amber Clayton) during their honeymoon.
Alice's dream marriage to the dashing, wealthy and successful Joe Chambers is plagued by his numerous indiscretions.
After a woman discovers that her husband has been murdered, the investigation reveals that the victim may have been living a double life.
When it appears one of their own shot an unarmed man on a Boston subway platform, the team must find the real killer while clearing their detective's name.
Jane and Maura find themselves in the world of competitive bass fishing when a tournament-leading fisherman is killed; Frankie loses a bet.
Jane and Maura are called out to the BCU body farm when a murder victim is found buried among the research corpses; Angela keeps secrets from Jane.
The murder of a notorious thief sends Jane and Maura into the world of art heists and forgery; Jane must deal with an FBI agent who is interested in her case; Angela has a new man in her life.
The murder of a crime tech shocks the team; Maura is suspended from her position; Jane is determined to catch the killer and clear the department, so Maura can be reinstated.
Kidnapping victim Elizabeth Smart, family members and law-enforcement officials discuss the 2002 abduction that made national headlines and the efforts made to find and save her.

Kidnapping victim Elizabeth Smart tells the story of traveling to Southern California with her abductors, their return to Utah, and how the television show "America's Most Wanted" played a role in her rescue.

New information comes to light about Jodi Arias and the murder of her ex-boyfriend, Travis Alexander, as her former cellmates and closest confidants give firsthand accounts of their time behind bars with the murderess.
Four women belonging to cult leader Jim Jones' inner circle help plan the 1978 Jonestown massacre in Guyana, which leaves more than 900 people dead.
Chandra Torres sits down with fellow kidnapping victim Elizabeth Smart to discuss life in captivity at the hands of a master manipulator and murderer.
Chronicling the lives and work of conservation officers in America.

In Kenya, former 🥊 [UFC] UFC Champion Luke Rockhold faces off with the Maasai warriors, and tests himself with Mario before going into the deep wilderness to discover an animal that eludes them and then reappears.

Mario goes as far north as he can and once he's there, he goes a little further; he finds himself in one of the most remote parts of the world, exploring an unknown landscape; there's reindeer, arctic char and more.

After Justin Harris severely breaks his leg deep in a remote, Utah canyon, it's up to his brother Jeremy to climb out for help. Clawing his way through icy pools of water and up rock faces, pushes Jeremy to his limit.

Ed Rosenthal set out for a short hike in Joshua Tree National Park, but in the heat of the day he became turned around and lost. His six-day ordeal of survival in blazing temperatures with no food or water is nothing short of miraculous.
Someone on a snowmobile takes an unexpected turn; a motocross presentation goes wrong.
A dangerous rally runs through the mountains of Colorado.
Humberside Search and Rescue rush to Thornwick Bay to help a man who has suspected head and spinal injuries; in the Lake District, Maria's walking holiday is cut short.
Brave volunteers face treacherous landscapes to rescue those in peril across the UK.
A freak car accident in Cumbria leaves Richard fighting for his life; in Hampshire, horse rider Pat takes a nasty fall when her animal is spooked.

While solo climbing Mt. Goddard, a remote peak in the California Sierra, Gregg Hein's leg is crushed by a boulder, and he's sent careening down the mountain. Barely able to stop his fall, he's now faced with a horrific compound fracture.

After his leg is crushed by a boulder, Gregg Hein is stranded on a high Sierra peak with an infected compound fracture. Knowing he won't be reported missing for days, Gregg attempts to crawl off the mountain and rescue himself.
As inevitable as natural disasters seem, Mother Nature often gives vital clues humans ignore; takes a close look at avalanches and what humans can learn about how, where, and why they strike.

A fell runner breaks her leg in the Ochil Hills and must remain calm while rescue teams figure out the best way to extract her; in Portscatho, a dog gets stuck on a cliff; the Keswick Mountain Rescue team help some injured walkers.

In Yorkshire, Neil needs urgent attention after a fall from his motorbike; the medics head to the banks of Ullswater when a walker goes into a cardiac arrest; in Berkshire, Darran suffers nasty burns in an accident lighting a bonfire.
A 39-year-old man has crashed his bike 15 kilometers south of Auckland city, and an elderly man has collapsed while walking; he is unable to speak properly and is incoherent at Waiheke Island.
A 70-year-old man who has a history of heart failure is trapped under a kayak at sea; a two-year-old falls off her mini quad-bike.
Two fishermen survive a night at sea by clinging to an Esky, and the rescue makes international headlines; a man loses his ring fingers when his motorbike crashes.
Women are not well represented in the police, but they play a key role in India and Palestine where they deal with special cases involving women.
Mark Seidenfeld thrives in Kazakhstan before crossing a local power broker and ending up in a freezing Siberian prison.
In Texas, Mike and Frank tackle a mega pick at the first Dr. Pepper bottling plant; the guys engage in tough negotiations in a 50,000 square-foot warehouse.
A Maryland car fanatic opens the doors to his late father's massive collection; after Robbie takes a joyride back to the '70s, Mike revs up a retro British taxi.
Mike and Frank make a killer backroom deal after winding up at the home of a former arms dealer and her Judo-champion husband.
Mike bids on the rusty frame of a famous hot rod; Mike and Frank agree to invest in a restoration project.
Mike and Frank have their work cut out for them on a huge property with more custom 1932 Fords than they have ever seen in one place; Danielle takes on an important military mission.
Teeming with taxidermy, Ron's Illinois home is like "Pet Sematary" meets the Natural History Museum.
Danielle splurges on the skeletal remains of a rare 1935 Indian Chief and then tries to sell it at the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally.
Alli takes up poker, and gambles with her future and her relationship with Dave.
Katie must choose between friendship and her feelings for Drew.
Katie and Marisol expose each other's secrets while fighting over Drew.
Fiona feels left behind when Holly J. and Anya ditch her for the prom.
Graduation approaches; Holly J. faces surgery; Fiona struggles with her demons; Katie deals with Drew's expectations for sex.
The seventh-grade class wants to impeach Stephanie (Nicole Stoffman).
Spike (Amanda Stepto) is given an egg to look after in a simulation of baby care. With Billy Parrott.
Lucy (Anais Granofsky) is delighted when she attracts a teacher's (Marcus Bruce) appreciative notice.
Joey (Pat Mastroianni) plans to test a new student's (Cathy Keenan) "fast" reputation.
Spike's and Shane's (Amanda Stepto, Billy Parrott) parents meet to discuss the baby.
Caitlin is determined to win the lead in the school play despite her epilepsy.
Jenna needs a break from the baby, and hopes to return to school and lead a normal life.
A visit from Child Services may push Jenna and K.C. to their breaking point.
Drew's fight training is the only thing keeping him together.
Alli grows tired of sneaking around and hopes that her parents can accept Dave.
Eli goes off his medication and begins to behave erratically.
Eli stretches the limits of his sanity in a bid to get Clare back; Imogen is interested in Eli.
Alli plans a special night so that she can break the news to Dave about their summer apart.
Drew is wary when Bianca and Vince start to appear in his space again.
Different couples must make difficult decisions on their prom night.
The world is morphed into an unrecognizable place where the library never existed; Baird brings the librarians together in an attempt to prevent the bleak, new world from becoming the new reality.
Someone is killing off potential Librarians, and it's up to Flynn Carsen and his new Guardian, Colonel Eve Baird, to save the three that are left.
The Serpent Brotherhood is trying to return magic to the world; Flynn, Colonel Baird, and the potential Librarians must stop them before it's too late.
The librarians' first solo mission hits a snag when Baird loses the others in a mysterious labyrinth that magically exists below the skyscraper of a modern corporation.
When the Serpent Brotherhood wants to kill Santa, the librarians must rescue him and help him accomplish the secret purpose of Christmas.
A caretaker beneath a metropolitan library protects magical artifacts from those who would use them to do evil.
When dissension threatens the group, Baird takes the Librarians to a charismatic self-help guru's team-building camp on the edge of a forest where people have been mysteriously disappearing.

Cassandra decides to take a vacation after she freezes up during a mission; during her visit to Havenport, labeled the "Safest Town in America," Cassandra believes things may not be as ideal as they seem.
When a town's Civil War re-enactment is plagued by ghosts, the Librarians have to uncover the truth of what really happened there over 100 years ago.
After switching bodies with a 28-year-old slacker named Jeff, Jenkins enlists the help of Jeff's hapless friends to find his way back into the Library to correct the mistake.

It's time to choose the Librarian who will be tethered to Baird, but no one can decide, so the Library comes up with a trial during which the Librarians will be reduced to their most primal selves and abandoned in nightmarish landscapes.

Each episode gives viewers an inside look at television, film and music, including interviews with each industry's biggest stars. Over the years, many celebrities have "broken their silence" regarding various scandals or tragedies with hosts and correspondents from "ET." In addition to covering breaking news, the show visits sets of movies and TV shows and heads to the red carpet to cover awards shows and other major events. Airing daily since 1981, "Entertainment Tonight" is the template by which many other entertainment newsmagazines are based.
Taking a closer look at some of the people, places, and things brought to viewers every weekend.

Successful forensic psychologist Alex Cross (Morgan Freeman) discovers that his niece has gone missing. Once he consults with police Detective Nick Ruskin (Cary Elwes), Cross believes that the disappearance is the work of an insane killer known as "Casanova." Meanwhile, Dr. Kate McTiernan (Ashley Judd) is kidnapped by this criminal and witnesses many other imprisoned women in his lair. After narrowly escaping, McTiernan teams up with Cross to try to apprehend the deranged Casanova.

Dr. Louis Creed and his wife, Rachel, relocate from Boston to rural Maine with their two young children. The couple soon discover a mysterious burial ground hidden deep in the woods near their new home. When tragedy strikes, Louis turns to his neighbor Jud Crandall, setting off a perilous chain reaction that unleashes an unspeakable evil with horrific consequences.

After surviving a car accident, Michelle (Mary Elizabeth Winstead) wakes up to find herself in an underground bunker with two men. Howard (John Goodman) tells her that a massive chemical attack has rendered the air unbreathable, and their only hope of survival is to remain inside. Despite the comforts of home, Howard's controlling and menacing nature makes Michelle want to escape. After taking matters into her own hands, the young woman finally discovers the truth about the outside world.

On the eve of D-Day, American paratroopers drop behind enemy lines to penetrate the walls of a fortified church and destroy a radio transmitter. As the soldiers approach their target, they soon begin to realize that there's more going on in the Nazi-occupied village than a simple military operation. Making their way to an underground lab, the outnumbered men stumble upon a sinister experiment that forces them into a vicious battle against an army of the undead.

For Dan Gallagher (Michael Douglas), life is good. He is on the rise at his New York law firm, is happily married to his wife, Beth (Anne Archer), and has a loving daughter. But, after a casual fling with a sultry book editor named Alex (Glenn Close), everything changes. Jilted by Dan, Alex becomes unstable, her behavior escalating from aggressive pursuit to obsessive stalking. Dan realizes that his main problem is not hiding his affair, but rather saving himself and his family.

When a cockroach-spread plague threatens to decimate the child population of New York City, evolutionary biologist Susan Tyler (Mira Sorvino) and her research associates rig up a species of "Judas" bugs and introduce them into the environment, where they will mimic the diseased roaches and infiltrate their grubby habitats. So far so good ... until the bugs keep on evolving and learn to mimic their next prey -- humans.

Factory worker Trevor Reznik (Christian Bale) suffers from insomnia so severe that his condition has taken its toll on his weight and his mental health. When Trevor unintentionally causes an on-the-job accident that horribly injures a coworker (Michael Ironside), he begins to become even more troubled. Despite a relationship with Stevie (Jennifer Jason Leigh), a pretty prostitute, Trevor descends further into paranoia, blaming his problems on an enigmatic figure named Ivan (John Sharian).

Playful Pee-wee Herman (Paul Reubens) operates a fantastical farm with talking animals and hot-dog trees. One day, after a giant tornado hits, Pee-wee finds a circus has landed in his yard. He befriends the manager, Mace Montana (Kris Kristofferson), and develops a crush on a trapeze performer (Valeria Golino), even though he already has a fiancée (Penelope Ann Miller). Pee-wee tries to excite the town about the new circus, but most of the residents want it gone and harass Pee-wee because of it.
Chaos ensues when a meteor hits the Earth carrying alien life forms that give new meaning to the term survival of the fittest.

Cone-headed extraterrestrials Beldar (Dan Aykroyd) and Prymaat (Jane Curtin) find themselves in New Jersey after a recon mission for their home planet of Remulak goes awry. Stranded, they are forced to live as typical suburban humans. Beldar gets a job, and daughter Connie (Michelle Burke) grows up to be a typical, if oddly shaped, teenager. When INS agents start investigating the family and Beldar receives sinister orders from Remulak, the Coneheads must decide where their allegiance lies.

In the wake of her mother's death in a mental institution, detective Rita Veder (Angela Bassett) is assigned to a baffling serial murder case. After examining the crime scene -- a corpse-filled ship found adrift at sea -- Rita meets Maximilian (Eddie Murphy), a smooth-talking Caribbean playboy determined to romance her. When Rita begins suffering from crippling hallucinations, she calls upon Dr. Zeko (Zakes Mokae), an occultist who suspects a vampire is on the loose.

Wren (Victoria Justice) is a high-school senior who can't wait to get away from her dysfunctional family. On Halloween, Wren's mother decides to go out with her much-younger boyfriend, leaving Wren to look after little brother Albert. When Wren is distracted by an invitation to the party of the year, Albert disappears into a sea of trick-or-treaters. Enlisting the aid of her sassy friend, April (Jane Levy), and two other classmates, Wren sets out on a frantic search for her sibling.

In 1971 two oil tankers collide off the coast of San Francisco, spilling millions of gallons of crude oil and creating an environmental disaster. Against all odds, trucking and construction entrepreneur Charlie Walker secures a lucrative contract to clean the coastline. However, he also finds himself fighting institutional racism from the very company that hired him.

The 20-year arms dealing career of Queens, N.Y., outcast Yuri Orlov (Nicolas Cage) serves as a window onto the end of the Cold War and the emergence of worldwide terrorism. He finds himself reassuring his more ethically challenged younger brother, Vitaly (Jared Leto), while adeptly sidestepping the pursuit of federal agent Jack Lawrence (Ethan Hawke). The globetrotting arms dealer also pursues the woman of his dreams, supermodel Ava Fontaine (Bridget Moynahan).

When a student writes the police code for homicide, 187, inside a textbook owned by teacher Trevor Garfield (Samuel L. Jackson), he feels threatened. The principal dismisses the incident, but, soon after, Trevor is stabbed by the same student. Fifteen months later, a physically and emotionally scarred Trevor relocates to California and takes up substitute teaching. To his dismay, his new school is as full of dangerously undisciplined students as the last one, driving Trevor over the edge.

Ever since they were kids, Sincere (Nas) and Buns (DMX) have lived life close to the edge, doing whatever it takes to survive. As adults, they build up their kingdom of crime on drug dealing and robbery. But Sincere grows weary of the criminal lifestyle and joins a black Muslim religious group. Buns, on the other hand, sinks deeper into criminality and faces serious prison time. The cops offer him a deal, however -- assassinate the head of the Muslim group, and he will go free.
After eight years in prison, G (Jayceon Taylor) is released and returns to his old ways on the streets -- until he starts to fall for a policewoman (Shari Headley).

At age 72, legendary trainer Ray Arcel (Robert De Niro) comes out of retirement to coach world-class Panamanian boxer Roberto Durán (Edgar Ramírez). Arcel becomes a mentor to the ferocious fighter, convincing him that winning ultimately comes down to strategy. After scoring knockout after knockout, Duran prepares for a bout against Sugar Ray Leonard, the undefeated lightweight champion. Five months later, on Nov. 25, 1980, the two titans meet for an infamous rematch that makes boxing history.
A small-time thief (Milo Ventimiglia) makes a big score and tries to keep it from his ex-partner, his ex-wife and other greedy sorts.

Seemingly everyone wants a piece of his enormous farmstead, including high-ranking government men, McLintock's own sons and nearby Native Americans. As McLintock tries to juggle his various adversaries, his wife, who left him two years previously, suddenly returns. But she isn't interested in her husband -- she wants custody of their daughter.

Danny Bryce (Jason Statham), one of the world's deadliest special-ops agents, returns from self-imposed exile after his mentor, Hunter (Robert De Niro) is captured. Danny reassembles his former team of skilled commandos to launch a rescue mission, and also to infiltrate the highly feared military unit, the British Special Air Service. The mission will not be easy, for Danny and his team must cut their way through Spike (Clive Owen) and a team of assassins known as the Feather Men.

Mercenary leader Barney Ross and his loyal men take on what they think is a routine assignment: a covert operation to invade the South American country of Vilena and overthrow its dictator. But, when they learn that the job will be a suicide mission, they must choose redemption or the destruction of their brotherhood.

But things go terribly wrong, compelling the mercenaries to seek revenge for a comrade's murder. With the odds against them, Barney and his team are hell-bent on payback and cut a path of destruction through opposing forces, only to encounter an unexpected threat: six pounds of weapons-grade plutonium.

Years ago, Barney Ross co-founded the Expendables with Conrad Stonebanks. After Stonebanks became an arms dealer, Ross was forced to kill him -- or so he thought. Now, Stonebanks is back, and he's on a mission to end the Expendables. Ross decides that the way to fight old blood is with new blood, so he assembles a team of younger, faster, more tech-savvy recruits. The battle to topple Stonebanks becomes a clash of old-school methods vs. high-tech expertise.

Young Cole Sear (Haley Joel Osment) is haunted by a dark secret: he is visited by ghosts. Cole is frightened by visitations from those with unresolved problems who appear from the shadows. He is too afraid to tell anyone about his anguish, except child psychologist Dr. Malcolm Crowe (Bruce Willis). As Dr. Crowe tries to uncover the truth about Cole's supernatural abilities, the consequences for client and therapist are a jolt that awakens them both to something unexplainable.

Popular recurring segments on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon.
Jimmy Fallon challenges celebrity guests to a variety of games: Box of Lies, Charades, Pup Quiz, Pictionary, Egg Roulette, Catchphrase, True Confessions and more on The Tonight Show.

Featuring easy makeup and fashion hacks, lighthearted pranks and funny observations; entertaining and positive shows about everything trending right now.
With Violet's support, Betty comes to St. Josephine to take back her land and reunite with her daughter; Ralph Angel speaks before the USDA; Micah meets with an investor; Nova receives sad news.

Landing in jail for a petty theft crime, Alvin finds himself sharing a cell with John Jaster, the incarcerated half of the pair of high-tech thieves responsible for the missing gold. His partner, Bristol, is still at large. Alvin wants only to get out of prison and start fresh with his girlfriend, Lisa, and when the Feds, led by U.S. Treasury investigator Clenteen, set him loose on a sketchy deal, he thinks his luck has changed. Alvin has his freedom and the Feds have found their bait.

Drug tycoon Nino Brown (Wesley Snipes) and his minions, known collectively as the Cash Money Brothers, have rapidly risen to the top of the New York City narcotics trade. Under Nino's heartless leadership, the drug operation has grown into a multimillion-dollar empire. Scotty (Ice-T) and Nick (Judd Nelson), two police officers who know their way around the streets of Harlem, aim to bring Nino and his cohorts down. To do so, though, they'll have to play by Nino's rules and go undercover.

After tracking down and arresting Earl Talbot Blake (John Lithgow), a psychotic hit man, rookie Los Angeles police officer Nick Styles (Denzel Washington) is hailed as a hero. Several years later, Styles' life appears perfect: He has married his girlfriend, started a family and risen to the position of assistant district attorney. However, his world is turned upside down when Blake escapes from prison with plans to exact brutal and well-calculated revenge.

Clyde Shelton is an honorable family man, until the day his wife and daughter are murdered in a home invasion. He hopes for justice, but a rising prosecutor named Nick Rice cuts a deal with one of the killers in exchange for testimony. Ten years later, that man is found dead.

Police drama about a veteran officer who escorts a rookie on his first day with the LAPD's tough inner-city narcotics unit. "Training Day" is a blistering action drama that asks the audience to decide what is necessary, what is heroic and what crosses the line in the harrowing gray zone of fighting urban crime. Does law-abiding law enforcement come at the expense of justice and public safety? If so, do we demand safe streets at any cost?

When flight attendant Jackie Brown (Pam Grier) is busted smuggling money for her arms dealer boss, Ordell Robbie (Samuel L. Jackson), agent Ray Nicolette (Michael Keaton) and detective Mark Dargus (Michael Bowen) want her help to bring down Robbie. Facing jail time for her silence or death for her cooperation, Brown decides instead to double-cross both parties and make off with the smuggled money. Meanwhile, she enlists the help of bondsman Max Cherry (Robert Forster), a man who loves her.

A former assassin, known simply as The Bride (Uma Thurman), wakes from a coma four years after her jealous ex-lover Bill (David Carradine) attempts to murder her on her wedding day. Fueled by an insatiable desire for revenge, she vows to get even with every person who contributed to the loss of her unborn child, her entire wedding party, and four years of her life. After devising a hit list, The Bride sets off on her quest, enduring unspeakable injury and unscrupulous enemies.

The Bride (Uma Thurman) picks up where she left off in volume one with her quest to finish the hit list she has composed of all the people who have wronged her, including ex-boyfriend Bill (David Carradine), who tried to have her killed four years ago during her wedding to another man. Leaving several dead in her wake, she eventually tracks down Bill in Mexico. Using skills she has learned during her assassin career, she attempts to finish what she set out to do in the first place.

It is the first year of Germany's occupation of France. Allied officer Lt. Aldo Raine assembles a team of Jewish soldiers to commit violent acts of retribution against the Nazis, including the taking of their scalps. He and his men join forces with Bridget von Hammersmark, a German actress and undercover agent, to bring down the leaders of the Third Reich. Their fates converge with theater owner Shosanna Dreyfus, who seeks to avenge the Nazis' execution of her family.

Stuntman Mike is a professional body double who likes to take unsuspecting women for deadly drives in his free time. He has doctored his car for maximum impact; when Mike purposely causes wrecks, the bodies pile up while he walks away with barely a scratch. The insane Mike may be in over his head, though, when he targets a tough group of female friends, including real-life stuntwoman Zoe Bell (who served as Uma Thurman's double in "Kill Bill"), who plays herself.

ALF and his friends portray an amusing fight against injustice in a jazzed-up version of the classic tale, "Robin Hood", which is considered one of the best in English folklore.
ALF and his friends showcase the magic of true love, a silly battle of good vs evil, and a strangely funny twist in a gender-reversed version of "Sleeping Beauty".
ALF and his friends give a glass-shattering twist to the classic, "Cinderella", by bringing rock 'n' roll, an absent-minded father, and a different kind of fairy godmother into the picture.
Ichabod Crane works with a newspaper, and seems to have solved the mystery of the headless horseman in ALF's version of "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow."
Jack uses magical beans to revive his mother's motel business and ends up finding love in an Alfred Hitchcock version of "Jack and the Beanstalk."
Staggering under failures, the Aladdin brothers wind up in a desert amid a tour and stumble upon a magic lamp that houses a genie in a modern retelling of a popular middle-eastern folk tale.
ALF and his friends present Rapunzel as a long-haired rap-singing beauty with vision-correcting tears in an amusing version of the classic fairytale.
ALF and his friends turn "Rumpelstiltskin" into a modern-day work of detective fiction wherein the protagonist seeks an investigator's help to find out the name of a mystical creature.
In a strangely entertaining version of "The Princess and the Pea", ALF and his friends present the story of a prince who finds love while pursuing comedy as a career.
John Henry becomes an extraordinary chef pitted against a cooking machine in ALF's entertaining version of the popular American folklore.
In an entertaining version of "The Three Little Pigs", ALF and his friends stick to the central plot of young piggies trying to build the best kind of houses.
ALF goes down an elevator shaft instead of a rabbit hole, and enters a magical place to find all kinds of weirdos in his version of "Alice in Wonderland."
ALF and his friends add their own twist to "Peter Pan", the story of a boy who lives in a magical land, never grows up, and befriends three children of a family in the real world.
ALF and his friends present their revamped version of the German classic, "Hansel and Gretel", wherein a brother-sister duo must save themselves from a dreadful witch.
With little help, ALF must take on a powerful witch after he winds up in the land of Oz in an entertaining version of "The Wizard of Oz."
In a retelling of "The Elves and the Shoemaker", a mediator shows up to make things right when a poor guy becomes greedy and exploitative toward some happy helpers.
ALF and his friends give the classic tale, "The Emperor's New Clothes", a hilarious makeover wherein a clothing freak emperor gets duped in the name of fashion.
Goldie Locks does not realize what she is getting herself into by using someone else's house for her enjoyment in ALF'ss version of "Goldie Locks and the Three Bears."
ALF and his friends present their entertaining version of "Little Red Riding Hood", a 17th-century European classic tale about an unsuspecting little girl who faces a scary predator.
ALF and his friends take the rivalry between Snow White and the evil queen to another level in an exciting version of the classic tale.
An Indiana Jones-like character wishes to help King Midas with the cursed touch, but there are people who don't want that to happen in ALF's amusing version of the classic tale.
The Tanners meet ALF for the first time when he crashes into the family's garage. Stars Max Wright, Anne Schedeen.
A family is forced to fight demonic creatures for survival after they move into a remote mill house in Ireland.
A woman finds a VHS tape that shows a series of gruesome tales.
Once a victim of vicious bullying, a teenage girl (Sierra McCormick) rises from the grave to punish the tormentors of a new student (Ronen Rubinstein) at a remote school.
Two scientists (Jed Brophy, Jeffrey Thomas) and a young psychic (Laura Petersen) encounter a demonic spirit at a haunted New Zealand farmhouse.
A disillusioned field surgeon who is suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder makes a man out of body parts and brings him to life in a Brooklyn loft.

Hoping for a joyful family reunion, Matt and his wife pay a surprise visit to the home of his estranged brother, Steve, to celebrate Christmas. To their shock, they soon learn that Steve has a hostage in his basement -- a man he claims is the devil.
A troubled widow (Essie Davis) discovers that her son is telling the truth about a monster that entered their home through the pages of a children's book.

Tinja is a 12-year-old gymnast who's desperate to please her image-obsessed mother. After finding a wounded bird in the woods, she brings its strange egg home, nestles it in her bed and nurtures it until it hatches. The creature that emerges soon becomes her closest friend and a living nightmare, plunging Tinja into a twisted reality that her mom refuses to see.
Las comunidades unen sus fuerzas en la última batalla contra los Salvadores. Negan ha conseguido entregar a Rick un mapa con instrucciones, para así tenderle una emboscada.
Rick y su grupo hacen un viaje arriesgado a Washington, D. C. para buscar los artefactos que necesitarán para construir la civilización que él y Carl imaginaron.
Las comunidades se unen para restaurar un puente que facilite la comunicación y el comercio, pero alguien resulta gravemente herido. Además, varios Saviors han desaparecido.
Una desaparición misteriosa pone en peligro los planes para el futuro de Rick y divide al grupo mientras construyen un puente.
La visión de Rick de un futuro civilizado se ve amenazada por un cúmulo de traiciones y agravios pasados que nunca fueron vengados ni perdonados.
Rick se ve obligado a enfrentar el pasado en su intento por proteger a las comunidades y el futuro que Carl y él concibieron.
Seis años después de la desaparición de Rick, un grupo recién llegado a Alejandría, liderados por la temperamental Magna, genera problemas a los habitantes de la comunidad.

Eugene está solo y en peligro, perseguido por una horda de zombis que, aparentemente, hablan. Mientras tanto, Michonne guía al grupo de Magna hasta Hilltop, donde esperan ser aceptados como nuevos miembros de la comunidad.

Daryl, Jesús y Aarón encuentran a Eugene, pero la horda de zombis parlantes los persigue incansablemente. Entretanto, en Alejandría, Negan escapa de su confinamiento porque a Gabriel se le olvida cerrar la puerta de su celda.
Los grupos individuales están convencidos de que pueden construir un futuro mejor por separado, pero la pérdida de un miembro los lleva a unir fuerzas. Se revela una amenaza perturbadora y peligrosa.

Daryl libera a Henry porque le estaba contando demasiadas cosas a Lydia y, después, interroga a la adolescente sobre su grupo. Entretanto, el grupo de Magna desobedece a Tara y se adentra por la noche en el bosque en busca de Luke.
El grupo de salvajes que lidera Alpha ataca Hilltop para recuperar a su hija. Mientras tanto, una misión en busca de suministros se convierte en una lucha entre la vida y la muerte.
Wherever your destination, traveling local or far, indoor or outdoor, you can be sure AccuWeather Weekend always has you covered.
Goes beyond the forecast to give you the how and why about stuff you wanted to ask about weather, space and science.

The Civil War is over, and the South has fallen, but Col. Jonas (Joseph Cotten) has a plan to revive the Confederacy. He raids a Union Army detail and walks away with valuable treasure that he intends to put to use raising another rebel army. Jonas needs to keep the treasure safe during shipment, so he places it in a coffin and forces saloon girl Claire (Norma Bengell) to play widow. Claire is unwilling to do her part, however, and puts herself in danger by opposing the dangerous Jonas.
Two Americans (Lee Van Cleef, Jack Kelly) lead Italian commandos on a World War II mission to secure a North African oasis.
An undercover man in Rome follows a crazed mob boss (Jack Palance) to a briefcase full of millions in stolen cash.

Lee Jeong Hwan, a fierce animal trainer, lives a chaotic daily life with his rebellious teenage daughter, Lee Su A, who is full of passion for dancing. One day, Su A becomes infected by a zombie virus that has swept across the globe.
A former secret agent, Ki-heon, is living in seclusion due to trauma. When he meets a cloned human, Seo Bok, his restless journey begins.
After surviving a bloody raid targeting a secret Witch Program, a girl goes on the run from the assassins tasked with finding and silencing her.
A former serial killer who has Alzheimer's disease must protect his beloved daughter from her psychotic boyfriend.
Trained in the Soviet Union, four special agents find themselves in constant danger after a traitor sells them out.

Detective Dong-geun investigates a murder with a note containing a date from 11 years ago found in the victim's mouth. The victim, a former military bully, forces Dong-geun to confront his own buried past.
After tracing a strange ailment to a remote gravesite, a team of supernatural experts soon discover what happens when you mess with the wrong grave.
Since 2017, the Navy has been releasing photos and videos of unidentified aerial phenomena, and ancient astronaut theorists suggest the images are nearly identical to accounts from centuries ago.
Charlie has to make a decision between keeping his group and being a sports psychologist for a baseball team.
Charlie, a baseball player with anger issues decides to return to therapy after a bad run-in with his ex-wife's new boyfriend.
The new Charlie deals with a ghost from his baseball-playing days when an unattractive woman he slept with shows up as a new patient.
A long-standing rivalry over who's a better therapist leads to Kate stealing one of Charlie's group patients.
Charlie challenges his group to do 36 hours of sleep-deprivation therapy so that their inhibitions come down.
One of Charlie's patients from his prison anger therapy group shows up on his doorstep; Jennifer gets back at Charlie by dating an ex-con.
Charlie starts covertly dating a brilliant coffee-shop barista who is a patient of Kate's; Charlie encourages his therapy group to call each other when facing moments of weakness.
Charlie falls for Jen's hot new business partner only to find she thinks therapy is a scam; Patrick asks Charlie to counsel the angry ghost of his mother.
Charlie evaluates the depth of his involvement in his patient's lives when he accidentally helps his patient hook up with a crazy woman.
Charlie gets an unexpected visit from his hypercritical father; Charlie attempts to help Lacey with road rage.
Charlie and Kate's sexual episode leads to complications when he innocently asks her to a movie; Sam kisses a girl and the picture winds up on a social media site.
Charlie gets an invitation to his sister's baby shower and asks Kate to come along. Patrick decides to tell Ed that his daughter is gay.
Charlie believes his father is faking Alzheimer's, and uses a hidden camera to spy on him. Patrick offers to help Nolan change his appearance to help his self-esteem.
Charlie begins a questionable romantic relationship with an ex-patient after the five-year mandatory waiting period runs out.
Charlie tries to persuade his father to join a choir of people his own age, a decision he later regrets. Lacey helps Patrick as an anger ally while he deals with a bully from high school.
Jennifer moves in with Charlie temporarily and Kate gets jealous.
Charlie tries to help his patient with a placebo pill that supposedly reduces anger; Jennifer asks Charlie to hang out with Kate.
Charlie gets involved with Sam's English teacher, he thinks her bad grade is based on his poor sexual performance; Lacey starts to have illicit romantic dreams about both Kate and Charlie.
Charlie runs into problems when CeeLo Green hires him as his personal therapist. Kate wants Charlie to drop CeeLo as a patient, because he is interrupting their time together.
Charlie and Kate face off as expert witnesses in the same trial; Charlie gives Nolan homework to get in touch with his feelings.
Martin has Charlie's daughter baptized behind Charlie's back.
Charlie dates Jennifer's business partner and finds out she has sexual anger issues; the support group tries to find a rich boyfriend for Lacey.
Lindsay Lohan comes to Charlie for therapy, and they begin a tumultuous relationship that ends up getting her in trouble.
Charlie's neighbors find out he's been having clients with anger issues meeting at his house; Kate goes with Jennifer to help find a dress for Sam.
When Sam finds out that her favorite horse is in equine therapy, Charlie uses that as a bonding exercise for his group.
Charlie inadvertently puts two patients together in a romantic relationship.
Charlie manages to persuade Kate to take Nolan on as her PA, but Nolan discovers more than Charlie would like to know. Meanwhile, Lacey is having problems in prison.
Charlie lets his father help him coach a high school baseball team; Kate takes over Charlie's group during his coaching gig.
Charlie's ex causes him problems with his group when she becomes one of his patient's life coach; Lacey helps Charlie's dad get a Facebook account.
Martin tells Kate that Charlie and Jennifer are getting back together; Nolan helps Ed as his anger buddy.
The family decides to go green, but it is much harder than they thought, and they sometimes realise you have to choose between saving the planet and saving your family.
Mr Peterson announces a new KAWT morning show featuring a reality show star as the co-host, but she threatens Nick and the other anchors' jobs in order to steal the spotlight.
Despite warnings from other co-workers, Nick gets stuck hosting a charity telethon, while Suzanne has to deal with a rich client's boring wedding plans.
When Suzanne's ex-husband wants to lower his monthly child support payments, Nick jumps at the chance while Suzanne has mixed feelings about Frank abandoning his own responsibilities.
After a concussion, Nick is advised to not go to bed for a few hours. To avoid all risks, he attempts to stay up all night.
When Suzanne's Mother comes to visit, she attacks Nick for being an inadequate husband, while hiding her true feelings of her own husband's inadequacy, until Suzanne and Terrence press her.
After a Guys' Night Out, Nick and his friends struggle to recollect the events that led to the disappearance of his wedding ring - and Kevin.
When Troy provokes a school bully, Kevin strikes up a friendship with his tormentor to avoid a beat down. However, Kevin is soon faced with a difficult decision.
Mr Peterson asks Nick to co-host his wife's charity walkathon, but Nick is soon put into an uncomfortable situation when he suspects that Mrs Peterson has stolen Marilyn's bracelet.
Lindsey and Kevin enter Nick into a Hand on a House contest, where finalists compete by seeing who can keep their hand on a house for the longest.
When a well-respected actor shadows Nick to prepare for an upcoming role as an anchor, but his methods turn out to be much more invasive that Nick had expected.
Nick attempts to have a night out with Lindsey, but when all she wants to do is to follow around a young celebrity DJ, Nick tries to teach her how a man should really treat her the way she deserves.
When Nick happens upon an old college pal, the unexpected meeting gives rise to a business plan that involves a sports star and an energy drink. The results, however, are not so bubbly.
Nick needs a new van for work, but Suzanne worries they are already too much in debt and cannot afford to buy a new one. It turns out Suzanne has some credit issues she has not revealed to Nick.
When Nick is invited to play in a celebrity golf tournament at Walt Disney World, Suzanne is disappointed she has to miss the family's first holiday.
Lindsey auditions to dance in a P-Nut music video, but considers quitting when she discovers that the choreographer is a drill sergeant and the other dancers are far more experienced.
Suzanne suspects Nick has a kid from a past relationship when she meets Kevin's new friend Nathan. He does everything Nick likes, eats and wears, and his mother is an old fling of Nick's.

Nick attempts to make a profit off an expensive set of African masks that Kevin bought at a yard sale, but instead, he becomes the victim of a larger scam. Lindsey receives advice about her upcoming date with her crush.
Suzanne gets caught dancing on a video that soon becomes a huge viral hit. Marilyn decides Lindsey needs to learn how to cook soul food.
Romantic complications ensue when Nick helps a shy colleague improve his love life. Meanwhile, a pinkeye epidemic keeps Lindsey away from school.
Lindsey makes a reality show about her family, but she thinks they are too boring - until Kevin finds Suzanne's gun in her bedroom and shows it to Troy, bringing real danger to the household.
When Suzanne crashes a night with Nick and his boys, Nick decides he needs to pay her back by showing up for spa treatments with Suzanne and her girlfriends to show her what it is like.
After Nick gets pocket-dialled by Suzanne and overhears her telling Gigi something personal, he gets back at Suzanne by fake pocket-dialling her.
When Nick tries to help Suzanne get over a childhood phobia, his secret plan accidentally causes her to relive the traumatic experience all over again.
When the house sitters next door begin acting irresponsibly, Nick and Suzanne question if they are being played for fools.
Nick refuses to give Lindsey money for a concert, so Lindsey resorts to stealing sixty dollars from Gigi's purse - but when Gigi discovers the missing money, she blames Kevin for the theft.
When a new buxom woman gets hired at the station, Nick's career is threatened. Suzanne takes matters into her own hands to save her husband's job.
Kevin's new career as a child actor quickly hits the skids when his big break causes him to get an even bigger head.
While speaking before Kevin's class for Career Day, Nick confuses the students by implying that building connections is more important than studying hard and getting good grades.
When the entire Kingston-Persons's clan plus guests end up at the house for a pot-luck Thanksgiving, Suzanne has to scramble to find the one item she was in charge of - the turkey.
Nick struggles to prove himself when he is promoted to co-host alongside the lazy, arrogant Brick Street.
Suzanne begins to force everyone in the family to tell the truth at all times after she catches Nick in a lie.
Yoh agrees to teach Haruna how to get a boyfriend but on the condition she doesn't fall in love with him.
Not too eager to watch Jan Di dancing with one of his best friends, Jun Pyo exits the ballroom and ends up taking out his frustrations by the poolside.
Making a rash choice, Jan Di tells her mother she has to go somewhere and runs off, heading toward Namsan Tower.
Jan Di's bike is set ablaze while she is attacked with water balloons and blasted with a fire extinguisher.
A psychic foresees that Jan Di will be losing something significant.
Jun Pyo intends to expel his best friend and Jan Di out of Shinhwa High School -- and out of F4.
Jan Di dashes to the hospital after being informed that Jun Pyo had been in an accident.
Yi-jung gets a frantic call from his mother threatening to commit suicide because of his father.
Yi Jung's mother frantically calls him threatening to commit suicide.
A note indicates that class has been moved to the science lab. The lab is unoccupied, but Jan Di waits, not realizing that the room is filling with fumes.

Impressed by high school student David's (Tobey Maguire) devotion to a 1950s family TV show, a mysterious television repairman (Don Knotts) provides him with a means to escape into the black-and-white program with his sister, Jennifer (Reese Witherspoon). While David initially takes to the simplistic, corny world of the show, Jennifer sets about jolting the characters with doses of reality that unexpectedly bring a little color into their drab existence.

Jane (Ashley Olsen) and Roxy Ryan (Mary-Kate Olsen) are teenage Long Island twins who find themselves on numerous misadventures when they trek into Manhattan on a school day. While the studious Jane intends to give an important speech in hopes of winning a scholarship, the more relaxed and carefree Roxy wants to track down her favorite New York City rock group. Trailing behind them, however, is Max Lomax (Eugene Levy), their school's obsessive truant officer.

Celebrated author and efficiency expert Frank Allen (Ryan Reynolds) has always lived in step with a well-planned series of lists and timetables. His wife (Emily Mortimer) decides to play a joke on him and sets his clock back 10 minutes, but the consequences are far greater than expected. As Frank's well-ordered existence unravels, he opens up to the randomness of life.

While attempting to seduce gorgeous lawyer Diane Lightson (Demi Moore), wealthy gadabout Chris Thorne (Chevy Chase) agrees to drive her to Atlantic City, N.J. But, when some reckless driving draws the attention of a deeply critical cop (John Candy), they and the flamboyant "Brazillionaires" (Taylor Negron, Bertila Damas) who tagged along end up in the court of a grotesque and vengeful judge (Dan Aykroyd), who has a special vendetta against the wealthy and erudite.

Gordie Boggs (David Arquette) and Sean Dawkins (Scott Caan) are best friends who operate a sewage truck and idolize pro wrestler Jimmy King (Oliver Platt). After Diamond Dallas Page (Diamond Dallas Page) dethrones their hero, Gordie and Sean embark on a mission to help King get his title back. When they finally track him down, however, they discover that King is not too keen on recapturing his former glory. Can the boys find a way to motivate the faded champ?

Former wrestler Sean Armstrong (Terry "Hulk" Hogan) takes a job as bodyguard and nanny to Alex Jr. (Robert Gorman) and Kate (Madeline Zima), the children of Alex Mason (Austin Pendleton). The kids receive little attention from their father and take out their energy in pranks on their babysitters. Despite their initial hostility, Sean and the children soon bond. When criminal Tommy Thanatos (David Johansen) kidnaps the kids to get his hands on a new computer chip, Sean must rescue them.

"I Am Sam" is the compelling story of Sam Dawson (Sean Penn), a mentally-challenged father raising his daughter Lucy (Dakota Fanning) with the help of a unique group of friends. As Lucy turns seven and begins to intellectually surpass her father, their close bond is threatened when their unconventional living arrangement comes to the attention of a social worker who wants Lucy placed in foster care.

When a British TV show becomes popular, an American network often makes its own version of the show. In this case, Lifetime is importing this series that pits four amateur cooks against one another as they compete for a cash prize. Each contestant prepares a meal for a dinner party -- with a unique theme, location and menu -- for the other competitors, who critique and score the cook. The contestant who earns the most points for his or her party wins the title of the host with the most and, more importantly, the money. Radio personality Todd Pettengill narrates the series.
Working mom Helen kicks off the week with an Arabian themed dinner party.
Ex-Royal Marine Ray is used to high-pressure situations, but this competition is a whole new level.
On her night, host dream analyst Joan, finally reveals to everyone what she does for a living.
Firefighter Paula is the quiet one of the group and everyone hopes that on her night she'll finally come out of her shell.
On the final night, 18-year-old journalism student Taylor has a retro 50s rock 'n' roll theme.

Tonight's host is dirt bike loving Sharon; Sharon calls herself a "yummy scrummy mummy" but it's the yumminess of her food that is questioned at the dinner.
Host Kyoko divides the group when she puts on a traditional Japanese menu; the kimono-clad guests are a little scared when Kyoko greets them with a board-breaking karate demonstration.

Confident adman David puts on his chef's jacket to cook up a fine dining menu; he doesn't think having a nice home is an advantage in the competition, but his guests are gobsmacked by David's designer home.

The competition is in and around Newcastle; the first host is 32-year-old ballroom dance instructor Stuart; Stuart hopes to dazzle his guests with his rainbow themed night and a colourful but healthy menu.
It is the second night from the Newcastle area, and it's Geordie geezer Adam's turn to host; Adam opts for fine dining and up-market gastropub food to try and wow his guests.

It is day three in Newcastle and horse obsessed nursing student Harriet is throwing a dinner party entirely themed around her equestrian hobby; she has got plenty of surprises in store for her guests.
Day four in Newcastle; videographer Jude hopes to win over her carnivorous guests with a decidedly experimental vegetarian menu; there is a distinct lack of vegetables.
It's the final night and Mo's turn to host with a menu of traditional South African dishes.
The first host in Essex is 46-year-old head teacher Corinna; she hopes her royal themed evening, regal cuisine and larger than life hosting will be enough to win her the cash prize.

The second host in Essex is 47-year-old money broker Paul who is out to impress with fine dining; he hopes his love of fancy restaurants and posh nosh will be reflected in his own cooking and be enough to win him the cash prize.
The third host in Essex is 43-year-old teacher and mother of four, Harmy, who hopes to spice up her guests' lives and bag the prize by serving up an authentic Punjabi feast.
The fourth to host in Essex is 25-year-old recruitment consultant Adam, who hopes to exceed expectations with a menu of posh nosh at his dad's house to win the final cash prize.

Monty travels across the middle of the country, from Wales to Norfolk. He comes across gardens for gnomes, much-loved, well-tended allotments and extravagant gardens that bankrupted their owners.

Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London's gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire.

Monty travels across the south-west of the country to visit some of Britain's most exotic gardens. On this journey, Monty also goes to some of the country's most historic gardens, as well as some challenging contemporary ones.

Monty's in the jewel garden showing which plants need protection from the elements now and which ones can be left until after the first frosts. He also plants out berried shrubs to help feed wildlife in the winter, harvests pumpkins and shows how to make use of fallen autumnal leaves.

After an extraordinary season, Monty's orchard has a bountiful harvest of apples and he gives advice on how to pick and store them. Frances Tophill makes a final visit to her shared allotment and joins in with the festivities at their annual show. Adam Frost visits the RHS garden Wisley where he meets the Curator to discuss the effects of summer. Nick Bailey investigates knotweed, one of the most pernicious weeds in the UK, Arit Anderson provides inspiration for colourful late season containers.

Monty and the team focus their attention on the loss of wildflower habitats in the UK and the part that gardeners can play in averting the resulting loss of wildlife. Adam Frost is in Lincolnshire to find out how crucial meadows are to supporting an ecosystem.

It is spring at Kew and after a long, dark winter, nature is coming back to life. Raymond makes his sublime version of rhubarb and custard and Kate finds out how a 12-year-old slave enabled vanilla to become the world's most popular flavour.

Summer has arrived at Kew and everything in Raymond Blanc and Kate Humble's garden is blooming. Butterflies and bees abound and there are new crops to tend, harvest and cook with. Everyone loves a carrot, particularly the carrot fly, so Raymond must protect his crop to ensure he has a good supply for his summer carrot stew.

It's autumn at Kew and the vegetable garden is set to produce a bumper harvest. Raymond Blanc and Kate Humble grow some autumnal favourites and cook them up. Kate finds out why the tomato was once considered to be a deadly poison.

The end of the year at Kew is fast approaching, winter is setting in, but some crops positively love the cold and Raymond learns how brassicas cope in this frosty season. Kate visits Kew's Millennium Seed Bank.

In Morocco, Monty discovers the wide variety of paradise gardens. He begins just outside the city of Marrakesh in an enormous royal walled meadow, The Agdal. From there he moves to the heart of the town where he comes upon a tiny garden where huge banana plants jostle with palms to create a secret paradise garden, a shelter from the busy world outside. And in another part of the city a rundown old palace has been turned into a stunning contemporary garden with a twist.

In Turkey Monty is dazzled by an extraordinary display of the Ottoman Empire's favourite flower, the tulip, and learns of its sacred significance. Travelling further East to India he encounters a new type of spirituality in the tomb gardens of the Mughal Empire. Stunning mausoleums were set in vast gardens as places where an earthly king could enter a divine paradise.

A new gardening year begins at Longmeadow and Monty reveals his new plans for the year as well as taking stock of any winter damage. As well as seasonal hints and tips he is embarking on a mission to reduce the use of plastic in his garden and starts by exploring alternative containers to use for seed sowing. Adam Frost brings his design expertise to a tiny backyard to demonstrate that no matter how small, with a bit of ingenuity, every space can count when it comes to gardening.

Christian religious leaders teach about Jesus and his various teachings on love, compassion and ethics.

South West contenders Paul Ainsworth and Nathan Outlaw, plus newcomer Simon Hulstone, kick things off with their starters, but which one is going to be first off the blocks? Will it be Paul with his 'Breakfast of Champions'; Nathan with hog's pudding with seaweed, potato terrine and mushroom ketchup; or Simon Hulstone with track and field - beetroot and goat's cheese?

The chefs cook their fish course, but which one will prevail? Will it be Paul Ainsworth with monkfish `Two Showings'; Nathan Outlaw with mackerel, horseradish and oyster sauce; or Simon Hulstone with `The Swimming Pool'?

The chefs cook their main course, but which chef will take gold? Will it be Paul Ainsworth with 'Wishful Chicken'; Nathan Outlaw with duck, barbecue monkfish, rosemary, samphire and asparagus; or Simon Hulstone with lamb with salted toffee pea mousse, shallot purée and asparagus?

It's the chefs' final chance to impress the veteran with their dessert dishes. Will it be Paul Ainsworth with 'Then and Now'; Nathan Outlaw with elderflower and lemon tart, with strawberry sorbet and meringues; or Simon Hulstone with 'Closing Ceremony'?

It's decision time on Great British Menu for the chefs from the South West region. One chef left the competition on the previous day and only two remain to cook their entire menus for the "Great British Menu" judges, Prue Leith, Matthew Fort and Oliver Peyton. The judges aren't easily pleased and only world-class cooking will do.

The 2012 competition enters its final week. The winners of the regional heats compete for a chance for their dish to be on the final banquet menu at a prestigious event hosted by Sir Steve Redgrave with a glittering guest list of British Olympians. Here, the finalists cook their starters, which will be tasted and scored by the "Great British Menu" judges and veteran judge Richard Corrigan.

The eight winners of the regional heats prepare to cook their fish dishes, which will be tasted and scored by the "Great British Menu" judges and veteran judge Marcus Wareing. Before they get into the kitchen, they must first learn whether they will all be cooking.
On day three, the chosen finalists cook their main courses, which will be tasted and scored by the "Great British Menu" judges and veteran judge Tom Kerridge.

It's desserts day in the finals, and the last chance for the competing chefs to impress the judges and veteran Angela Hartnett. After a hard-fought week, the end of this programme will see the judges finally reveal the winning four dishes which will make up this year's 'Great British Menu'.

This final programme follows the successful chefs in the run-up to the Olympic banquet at the Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich, as they make the painstaking preparations for what is one of the most important meals they will ever cook. The four winning chefs prepare an outstanding four-course menu for a truly Olympian guest list.

The spotlight is on Scotland. Returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway are all determined to get one of their dishes to the banquet. Will a witty take on spiced ham score highly, or will a warm chicken salad with a twist or a rabbit terrine come out on top? Veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE will be judging.

Returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway cook their fish dishes. Will a traditional Scottish soup, a chowder or a risky no-cook mackerel dish impress veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE?

The competition heats up as the three returning Scottish contenders, Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway, cook their main courses. An African inspired goat tagine, a beef dish inspired by a childhood cartoon and a duck dish with a comedy twist are dished up for veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE.

Scottish returning contenders Michael Smith, Tony Singh and Mark Greenaway have just one more chance to impress veteran judge Angela Hartnett MBE and win their place in front of the judges. Will a comedy custard pie, a sophisticated chocolate dessert or doughnuts inspired by a Scottish tradition come out on top?
Only one chef can make it through to the national finals to represent Scotland and cook at a special banquet at the Royal Albert Hall.

The curtain raises on the competition in the North West. How will Aiden Byrne's dish entitled `Mad as a Box of Frogs' go down with veteran Phil Howard? Will he trounce Mary-Ellen McTague's crab starter or will Chris Holland's `Oriental style beef broth with a twist' score more highly with Phil?

The North West chefs cook their fish courses. Will Aiden Byrne's "The Culinary Joke" - a take on a classic prawn cocktail - raise a laugh, or will Mary-Ellen McTague's dish of Dover sole or Chris Holland's "Gone Fishing" salmon dish prove winners?

The chefs cook their main course. Will Aiden Byrne's witty beef dish entitled 'Long Horn Beef with Noodle Pot' prove a winner, or will Mary-Ellen McTague's goat dish called 'Our Kid' raise a smile? Perhaps Chris Holland will score highly with his dish called 'A Tasting of Pork'.

It's the chef's last chance to impress before the final two are chosen to face the 'Great British Menu' judging panel. Which dessert will help get them through? Will it be Aiden Byrne's pineapple dish called 'The Sweet Burger', Mary-Ellen McTague's take on a trifle called 'Chamomile Lawn' or Chris Holland's dish called 'Going Bananas'?

In 701 BC, the brutal Assyrian army stood poised outside the walls of Jerusalem, ready to sack the city. Had they succeeded, Judaism would have died and Christianity and Islam might never have evolved.

Young couple Malcolm (Marlon Wayans) and Kisha (Essence Atkins) have just moved into their dream home. As they settle in, they learn that they're not alone -- not because the house is haunted, but because Kisha is possessed by a demon. Soon afterward, Malcolm is once again plagued by supernatural shenanigans -- only this time, it's not just the house that's haunted. A demon has attached itself to Malcolm, and shows no signs of letting go.
