At 18 years old, Jason receives a mandatory 10-year prison sentence after being caught with a package that contained illegal drugs, although he was unaware of its contents. His father, businessman John Matthews (Dwayne Johnson), is devastated. When Jason turns down a chance to lessen his sentence by manufacturing evidence to implicate someone else, John begs to be sent undercover instead, but the already dangerous venture turns deadly after he exposes a major player in the Mexican drug trade.
Police partners descend into the criminal underworld after they are suspended for assaulting a suspect on video.

A group of thieves assembles to pull off the perfect diamond heist. It turns into a bloody ambush when one of the men turns out to be a police informer. As the group begins to question each other's guilt, the heightening tensions threaten to explode the situation before the police step in.
A crew of retired crooks pulls off a major heist in London's jewelry district.

A case of mistaken identity puts a man named Slevin (Josh Hartnett) in the middle of a war between two rival New York crime lords: The Rabbi (Ben Kingsley) and the Boss (Morgan Freeman). While under the watchful eyes of Detective Brikowski (Stanley Tucci) and well-known assassin Goodkat (Bruce Willis), Slevin must quickly devise a plan to save his skin before his luck runs out.
A Mountie (Bob Steele) escorts a young woman bringing cash to her father in the wild.

Looking to reform the corrupt government of his Old West town, newspaperman Jeff Rose is running for mayor against officeholder Nard Lundy (Edward Andrews). Jeff's campaign lacks the incumbent's muscle and money, and his quest looks hopeless until the arrival of his father-in-law, Capt. Oren Hayes (Pat O'Brien). Joined by three fellow former Texas lawmen (Walter Brennan, Edgar Buchanan, Chill Wills), Oren and his daughter, Hannah, help Jeff fight back against his antagonist's dirty tactics.

Horse trader Roy Rogers has plans to breed his prize mare with legendary stallion Golden Sovereign. Unfortunately, scheming nightclub owner Brett Scoville (Jack Holt) has his eye on the same stud and steals the horse. Sovereign breaks free, however, and mates with Rogers's mare, eventually producing a spirited colt that Rogers names Trigger. When Sovereign is accidentally killed, Rogers is blamed for the crime, and he and Trigger must escape the law and track down the real killer.

After the Civil War, cavalryman Capt. Hunt tries to strike peace with Acoma, a Native American chief. However, Judge Wilcox and others provoke Acoma, arresting him and shooting his men, prompting revenge from the chief. In the ensuing battles, one of Acoma's sons is killed, enraging him further. Hunt must save Cherry, a dance hall girl caught up in the commotion, and try to find a way to end the bloody conflict with Acoma.

Dare Rudd (John Wayne) and Dinkey (Syd Saylor) are two friends who love to gamble. Needing money and shelter, they travel to Montana to visit Rudd's cousin, Tom (John Mack Brown), who owns a successful cattle ranch. Dare quickly falls for Tom's girlfriend Judy (Marsha Hunt), who convinces Tom to give Dare a chance to prove himself by running a cattle drive. When he loses the herd in a high-stakes poker game, Dare joins forces with Tom and Dinkey to get the cattle back.

Wrongly imprisoned for murder, John Brant (John Wayne) decides his only option is to escape from jail and clear his name by finding the true killer. After breaking out, he ends up on the run from Sheriff Parker (Bob Burns) and catches the attention of outlaw Bob Jones (Lane Chandler), who offers to let Brant into his gang. Needing all the help he can get, Brant agrees, but running with these bandits only gets him deeper into trouble -- while the real killer remains on the loose.

After pulling a bank heist in Mexico, the outlaw Rio (Marlon Brando) and his partner, Dad Longworth (Karl Malden), make a run for it, but Dad has bigger plans than freedom. He betrays Rio and absconds with the loot, and Rio ends up in prison. Years pass before Rio finally breaks free to enact his long-plotted revenge. Tracking Dad to California, Rio learns he's become a sheriff -- which is no deterrent -- but when Rio falls for Dad's stepdaughter, Louisa (Pina Pellicer), he has second thoughts.

Adopted by the wealthy rancher Arch Strobie, orphan Owen Daybright (Burt Lancaster) grows to be a respectable foreman on Strobie's ranch. Strobie's natural son, Lee (Robert Walker), is jealous of Owen and finally finds a way to undermine his upstanding brother. When Lee conceives an illegitimate child with Lily Fasken (Sally Forrest), who refuses to name him as the father, he tells her revenge-minded brothers that Owen is to blame, hoping they'll take his half-brother out of the picture.

Clint Belmet (Gary Cooper) is supposed to hitch up with a wagon train and head out west. But, to make the journey, he must first evade a criminal charge by convincing a brassy French girl, Felice (Lily Damita), to pretend to be his wife. Now serving as a trail guide, Clint journeys with Felice across the frontier, where a real romance starts to develop between them. But Clint will have to keep his wits about him when the settlers are attacked by outlaw Lee Murdock (Fred Kohler).

In a violent, near-apocalyptic Detroit, evil corporation Omni Consumer Products wins a contract from the city government to privatize the police force. To test their crime-eradicating cyborgs, the company leads street cop Alex Murphy (Peter Weller) into an armed confrontation with crime lord Boddicker (Kurtwood Smith) so they can use his body to support their untested RoboCop prototype. But when RoboCop learns of the company's nefarious plans, he turns on his masters.

Convinced of his irresistible appeal to women, Texas dishwasher Joe Buck (Jon Voight) quits his job and heads for New York City, thinking he'll latch on to some rich dowager. New York, however, is not as hospitable as he imagined, and Joe soon finds himself living in an abandoned building with a Dickensian layabout named Enrico Ratso Rizzo (Dustin Hoffman). The two form a rough alliance, and together they kick-start Joe's hustling career just as Ratso's health begins to deteriorate.

In a not-too-distant dystopian future, when man's most precious resource -- oil -- has been depleted and the world plunged into war, famine and financial chaos, the last vestiges of the law in Australia attempt to restrain a vicious biker gang. Max (Mel Gibson), an officer with the Main Force Patrol, launches a personal vendetta against the gang when his wife (Joanne Samuel) and son are hunted down and murdered, leaving him with nothing but the instincts for survival and retribution.
An aging rodeo rider (James Coburn) thinks more of himself than he does of his wife (Lois Nettleton), son and best friend (Slim Pickens).

In the quiet frontier town of Bitters, Wyo., a dispute between cattleman Blaise Starrett and farmer Hal Crane is about to boil over into a bloody feud. But the fighting takes a back seat to a new threat when a rogue cavalry captain, Jack Bruhn, rides into town with his band of thugs. Now, with the citizens of Bitters held hostage by Bruhn and his men, Starrett must somehow rescue his town and restore his broken reputation.

Thanks to his prowess with a gun, Dave Robles (Anthony Quinn) makes a place for himself in Mesa, becoming sheriff after out-dueling several gunfighters in a single day. But Robles, a Mexican, seethes over the town's racism, and is warned by kindly nurse Estella (Katy Jurado) that without his gun, he would not last very long. That theory is put to the test when the new sheriff injures his wrist fighting with Ed Bannister (Peter Whitney), who upon learning about it, challenges Robles to a duel.

During the 1912 Mexican Revolution, rebel leader Hector Córdoba (Raf Vallone) and his bloodthirsty revolutionaries slip across the Texas border and liberate a number of cannons from a U.S. Army fort. Under direct orders from General Pershing (John Russell), Captain Rod Douglas (George Peppard) heads into Mexican territory to face down Córdoba and get back the American cannons with the help of Mexican military officer Antonio (Gabriele Tinti) and alluring local Leonora (Giovanna Ralli).

A group of thieves rob a safe of $100,000 and plan to use the money to purchase some land near a proposed railway line. The crooks think they've gotten away with their crime, but they haven't figured on Sabata, a violent bounty hunter with no scruples and a strong desire for cash. He teams up with both his partner, Banjo, and a local bandit named Carrincha. Sabata's fast draw and quick wits make life hell for the thieves.

Gunslinger Sabata (Yul Brynner) allies himself with a group of wily Mexican revolutionaries scheming to overthrow Emperor Maximilian and expel the occupying Austrians from their homeland. Part of their plan involves stealing a shipment of gold and using it to purchase artillery. It won't be easy, however, as the gold is under the protection of the corrupt and sadistic Col. Skimmel (Gerard Herter). As Sabata pulls off the daring heist, he must take on dozens of enraged Austrian forces.

The third in a trilogy about the eponymous lone gunman, this one finds Sabata (Lee Van Cleef) working as a sharpshooter for a circus that's just stopped in an ailing one-horse town. The circus gig is only a front, however: Sabata is actually on the verge of robbing town mayor Joe McIntock (Giampiero Albertini). The mayor's been levying heavy taxes as part of a complex plan to defraud the community, but Sabata manages to rip him off first, only to discover that the money is counterfeit.

Apache Natives are after Ellen (Bibi Andersson), her baby, and her husband, William (Dennis Weaver). The family crosses paths with Jess (James Garner), a man who is trying to find out who killed his own wife, a Native American woman. He begins to travel with the couple, but the trailing Apaches soon chase them all into a canyon. Jess is able to escape the situation and alert nearby soldiers. But when a logging company comes near the rainforest, she sees that they do exist, and even accidentally shrinks one of them: a boy named Zak. Now her size, Zak sees the damage that the company does and helps Crysta to stop not only them, but an evil entity named Hexxus, who feeds off pollution.

Looking to escape her unhappy marriage, villainous femme fatale Bridget Gregory (Linda Fiorentino) convinces her husband, Clay (Bill Pullman), to sell cocaine, then steals the profits and runs out on him. She stops in a small town en route to Chicago, where she ensnares her next conquest, insurance man Mike Swale (Peter Berg). After getting a job at his insurance company, Bridget convinces Mike to run a scam -- but things take a deadly turn when she recruits him to help get rid of her husband.

Jobe (Matt Frewer) exists as a malevolent consciousness in virtual reality and seeks to discover the technology to hack into all the world's computers. Jobe contacts Peter (Austin O'Brien), who had been a friend during his corporeal existence, to assist him, but the young man realizes Jobe's evil intent. Peter calls on Benjamin (Patrick Bergin), a brilliant computer engineer, to help thwart Jobe's scheme for world domination, and a battle rages throughout cyberspace and in the real world.

When Helen, a London ad executive, is fired from her job and rushes out to catch a train, two scenarios take place. In one, she gets on the train and comes home to find her boyfriend, Gerry, in bed with another woman. In the second, she misses the train and arrives after the woman has left. Following the first scenario, Helen dumps Gerry, finds a new man and gradually improves her life. Under the second scenario, she becomes suspicious of Gerry's fidelity and grows miserable.

Austin, Texas, is an Eden for the young and unambitious, from the enthusiastically eccentric to the dangerously apathetic. Here, the nobly lazy can eschew responsibility in favor of nursing their esoteric obsessions. The locals include a backseat philosopher (Richard Linklater) who passionately expounds on his dream theories to a seemingly comatose cabbie (Rudy Basquez), a young woman who tries to hawk Madonna's Pap test to anyone who will listen and a kindly old anarchist looking for recruits.

The Roman Catholic Church combats a global rise in demonic possessions by reopening schools to train priests to perform exorcisms. Although nuns are forbidden to perform this ritual, a professor recognizes Sister Ann's gifts and agrees to train her. Thrust onto the spiritual frontline, she soon finds herself in a battle for the soul of a young girl who's possessed by the same demon that tormented her own mother years earlier.

Soon after the Montelli family buys a house in the Long Island suburb of Amityville, unsettling events begin to occur. Mysterious demons seem to infest the house, preying on abusive father Anthony (Burt Young) and ferociously religious mother Dolores (Rutanya Alda), who calls on family priest Father Adamsky (James Olson) for an exorcism. Teenage Sonny (Jack Magner) is drawn furthest into madness, abusing his younger sister, Patricia (Diane Franklin), and eventually exploding in a horrific fury.

Investigative reporter John Baxter (Tony Roberts) buys a notorious house in the Long Island suburb of Amityville, N.Y., in an attempt to prove that stories about its being inhabited by demons are fraudulent. But soon his daughter, Susan (Lori Loughlin), and her friend Lisa (Meg Ryan) are experiencing inexplicable terrors, while his estranged wife, Nancy (Tess Harper), and supernatural expert Elliot West (Robert Joy) fear that the evil has begun to spread outside the house's walls.

Landowners in 1817 Tennessee, John (Donald Sutherland) and Lucy Bell (Sissy Spacek) experience strange and terrifying events after fellow parishioners find John guilty of loan-sharking and his victim curses the Bell family. The incidents culminate in the daughter's (Rachel Hurd-Wood) apparent possession by demons.

Returning home after disappearing three years ago, former gunslinger Lorn Warfield (Glenn Ford) finds that an Apache raiding party has kidnapped his wife and children. Though he has renounced violence, he now takes up his gun and joins forces with his neighbor, Owen Forbes (Arthur Kennedy). Complicating matters, Forbes is engaged to Warfield's wife, who believed her husband was dead. As they pursue the Apaches, the two men are joined by an Indian trader, Jimmy Noble (Dean Jagger).

Jim Killian arrives in a small Arizona town hoping to establish a peaceful life as the local preacher, but he soon finds himself in the middle of a feud between sheep ranchers and cattlemen. Leloopa, a young Native American woman, pleads for Killian's help after her shepherd father is hanged by Coke Beck, the vicious son of the head cattle rancher. Killian must weigh his actions carefully lest he perpetuate the cycle of retribution and revenge.

At a U.S. Army fort in the Arizona Territory in 1881, an officer is murdered, and his beautiful young daughter is beaten, raped and strangled. Army lawyer Tom Cantrell (Jeffrey Hunter) defends the accused, African-American sergeant Braxton Rutledge (Woody Strode), a soldier who had once been under his command. Under questioning by Cantrell and the prosecutor (Carleton Young), multiple witnesses piece together the truth of what happened at the fort that day.

A Mexican-American War veteran, Jeremiah Johnson (Robert Redford), heads to the mountains to live in isolation. Woefully unequipped for the task at hand, Johnson is fortunate to come across a seasoned mountain man (Will Geer) willing to teach him the necessary survival tactics. As life continues in the mountains, Johnson finds himself a native bride (Delle Bolton) and an adopted son (Josh Albee). However, their peaceful existence is threatened when Johnson incurs the ire of the Crow Indians.

Patoso y sus desventuras lo llevan a un lugar desconocido. Allí conoce a las duendecillas, unas adorables criaturitas con enemigos que también pretenden meterse con los pitufos.
Todos los pitufos celebran una fiesta en honor a Pitufo Perezoso, y este se ve arrastrado a una absurda discusión sobre pintar los dedos de los pies de Gigantón de un brillante color mandarina.
Pitufo Genio y Goloso se enzarzan en una disputa sobre quién debe llevarse el mérito de la creación conjunta y accidental de un nuevo postre helado.
Una vanidosa duendecilla llamada Periwinkle secuestra a Vanidoso cuando su espejo mágico le dice que él es más guapo que ella.

En su plan para librarse de los Pitufos, Gargamel le lanza un hechizo a Gigantón y se disfraza de Pitufo. Creyendo que es un Pitufo, Gigantón está a punto de destrozar por completo la Aldea Pitufa hasta que Papá Pitufo acude con una cura.

Gargamel consigue transformar una colcha en una alfombra voladora, lo que hace inevitable que se produzcan accidentes. El resultado de uno de esos accidentes es que un trozo de la tela voladora acaba utilizándose como pañal para Bebé Pitufo.

Goloso tiene que escuchar cada día las quejas de los demás pitufos sobre la comida que prepara y cuando se da cuenta de que nadie valora lo que hace y además abusan de su nobleza, decide ponerse en huelga.

Katie is a first-time buyer and with practical and financial support from her dad, she tackles a rundown maisonette above bookies in London's trendy Crouch End, with the idea of living in one of the rooms and letting out the others.

A group of Indian POW (Prisoners of War) from the 1971 Indo-Pak war rebels against the Pakistani army and tries to escape from their captivity. Helping the group in the mission is Gaurav, the son of a former Army Major also held captive by the enemy.
A wealthy collegian (Kajol) falls in love with an heir apparent (Salman Khan), but her domineering cousin (Arbaaz Khan) orders her to end the affair.

On discovering that his death was a clerical mistake, Navin demands to be sent back to Earth to his friends and family. However, now he has to woo his fiancée all over again in another guise.
A sting operation results in the recovery of over 12 ounces of meth; an alarm goes off at a coffee shop; a report of a stolen vehicle at a gas station.
Two children are found riding on the top of a vehicle; a probation search on a lady who has outstanding warrants.

Police seek to take down a known drug house where they expect many arrests; deputies investigate a van parked after-hours in a school parking area; knives, bullets and marijuana are found in a suspicious car.
K9 Deputy Roberts and SED take down a marijuana grow and distribution operation run by a nine-time felon.
Deputies respond to a parolee who is locked in a residence, and known to have a weapon; a trained dog finds clues that a human would surely miss.
Police attempt to arrest a drug dealer; a young woman is found lying on the side of the road; officers try to catch people who are willing to buy alcohol for minors.
A Special Enforcement Detail executes a plan to catch some burglars who ransacked several homes; 911 caller reports that a woman broke into her car.
A deputy responds to a report of a dispute and finds a house destroyed by an intoxicated person.
A deputy responds to a fight at a popular bar; a person screams in a mall parking lot; two people are caught breaking into an apartment.
Police respond to a scene where a person at gunpoint is in a vehicle reported as stolen; a man reportedly jumps from a moving car; drugs are found in a vehicle that is stuck in a puddle.
Deputies search for four armed men who broke into homes and assaulted and robbed citizens; a deputy checks on the welfare of a woman who had recently given birth.
A man with multiple arrests for heroin possession talks about what life on the drug is really like.
A deputy follows two probationers into a known drug house; a water company worker contacting people about a water issue calls police about an extremely inebriated woman who fell down.

A vehicle fire on a highway; a man claims local citizens have been stealing from his store; Lake Tahoe's SnowGlobe Music Festival; a young woman with a substance abuse problem escapes custody while being treated at a hospital.
A driver runs off after being involved in an accident; patrolling a motel known for high drug activity; a fight breaks out at a gas station.
A deputy responds to a 911 call about a possible burglary; deputies answer a domestic violence call, where a man claims his wife choked him.
A bicycle stopped for not having lights leads to the discovery of a stolen 27 foot trailer and its parolee occupants; a brawl in a motel parking lot.

Responding to a domestic violence call, a deputy confronts an angry, non-compliant man who refuses to identify himself; deputies try to find out who shot a family's dog; a man is passed out in a truck.
A vehicle has no front license plates and an expired registration; two juveniles are reportedly intoxicated; deputies are informed when a child predator is release from jail.

A deputy is called to assist after a hit-and-run accident; a 911 caller reports a husband and wife fighting; deputies respond to a report from a mother that her vehicle was taken without permission by her daughter.
Deputies are flagged down over an alleged case of domestic violence; a man armed with a shotgun claims that people on his property are out to hurt him.
The search of a vehicle reveals drugs and a handgun; a homeless person trashes a woman's house.
Two people are discovered sleeping in a car in a high school parking lot; a deputy patrolling Lake Tahoe finds two women who fell out of their kayaks.
A probationer has a warrant out for his arrest; two occupants are found sleeping in a car behind a drug store; a deputy tries to stop teens from diving off a bridge.
Sheriff's Office Lake Tahoe boat patrol responds to reports of a possible boater under the influence.
A domestic violence call leads to a foot chase; a burglary in progress; a deputy finds heroin on a man who was stumbling in the road.
A deputy answers a 911 call about a lady stealing from a convenience store; a woman claims a prostitute solicited her husband in a restaurant.
A follow-up investigation into a robbery suspect with a felony warrant leads to a K during its job.
A woman's boyfriend is arrested for domestic violence; a search for two missing tourists; a naked transient occupies a supermarket bathroom for over an hour.

A woman hides in a store bathroom, claiming there is a man with a gun outside waiting to shoot her; a man is reported to have fallen off a cliff in South Lake Tahoe; two vehicles pulled over for speeding.
Deputies search for three young men reported to have committed a robbery at a gas station; a bear is reported to be wandering near peoples' homes; a domestic violence call.

A traffic stop reveals a man with stolen food and burglary tools, driving without a license; a deputy responds to a call about two intoxicated men; two men are reportedly fighting at a department store.
A theft at a supermarket ends in domestic violence; the Sheriff's Homeless Outreach Team responds to a disturbed woman; a tip about a heroin dealer comes from a confidential informant.

Crime reporter John Jones (Joel McCrea) is turning in nothing but dull copy. His editor, unhappy with his work, hopes a change of scenery will be the thing Jones needs to get back on track. Re-assigned to Europe as a foreign correspondent, Jones is very much out of his element. When he stumbles on a spy ring, he feels ill-equipped to unravel the truth alone, and he seeks help from a beautiful politician's daughter (Laraine Day) and an urbane English journalist (George Sanders).

Gina is a beautiful young woman who's still haunted by the accident that took her sight years earlier. Living in Bangkok with her husband, James, she undergoes a cutting-edge operation that restores the vision to her right eye. Now that Gina can see again, she slowly starts to realize that her newfound independence makes James feel jealous, threatened and insecure.

When a young girl goes missing, Yorkshire Post crime reporter Eddie Dunford (Andrew Garfield) becomes intrigued by a series of mysterious child murders that date back several years and mirror to the current case. He faces stiff opposition from the local police and his editor, Bill (John Henshaw). Eddie's troubles escalate when he becomes involved with a moody widow (Rebecca Hall) who has a mysterious connection to wealthy developer John Dawson (Sean Bean).
A policeman (Leslie Cheung) and a reformed gangster (Ti Lung) meet their dead friend's twin, employed by a New York mob boss.

His faith broken by many years fighting in the Crusades, a knight named Behman returns to Europe and finds it ravaged by the Black Plague. A dying cardinal orders Behman and his friend, Felson, to take an accused witch to a remote abbey, where monks will destroy her powers and end the pestilence. As Behman and five comrades undertake the dangerous journey, they come to realize that the prisoner is no ordinary girl, and evil forces await at the destination.

Majo Tonorio (Gina Rodriguez), a talented hip-hop artist, is offered a record deal from a sleazy producer. She faces a difficult choice between selling out for money or staying true to herself and her music.

Photographer George Cooper (John Heard) is documenting the lives of subterranean homeless people, a population that has mysteriously dwindled. After receiving information from a reporter, George becomes aware of a conspiracy theory about cannibalistic monsters lurking in the sewers. He teams up with the reporter, a policeman (Christopher Curry) and a priest (Daniel Stern) to fight two battles: one against the cannibals and the other against a corrupt government official.
The team learns a mother and baby disappeared at the same time two girls went missing, prompting thoughts that a serial killer may be to blame.
Halford visits a clairvoyant in hope of contacting his dead wife but, instead, finds himself communicating with a young girl who disappeared 20 years earlier.
Twenty years ago, QC Barrie was found tied up and dead in his car.
After a woman is beaten and falls into a coma, the UCOS enlists the help of an Asian community liaison officer to help find her attacker.
The case of a misidentified murder victim, reportedly kidnapped, has the team trying to find out what happened to a missing girl.
A tabloid editor asks UCOS to help prove a celebrity chef murdered her husband.
Halford must find the owner of a large, uncut red diamond found in a flat.
When Standing loses a poker game, a bookie offers to clear his debt in exchange for solving a mystery.
UCOS investigates the case of two boys abducted from a fishing lake.
A pathologist asks UCOS to reopen a 1987 case of a severed body found at Giston Mount.
The team investigates the murder of a young policewoman who once trained with Sandra; Brian's wife leaves him; Gerry learns he will be a grandfather.
The discovery of a fake painting in the Queen's art collection sends the UCOS team on a hush-hush mission to uncover the forger.
The UCOS team investigate the murder of a young peace protestor killed at the outskirts of a nuclear base in 1984 and realize that they may be in danger of exposing a Special Branch cover-up.
The members of a prestigious golf club come under suspicion when the UCOS team investigates a child murder.

Arthur Blake (Dominic Monaghan) is about to be executed by guillotine for the crime of grave robbing. But before he faces the blade, he agrees to confess to Father Duffy (Ron Perlman) in the hope that the priest might be merciful enough to spare his life. Arthur tells his life story to the priest, which begins with him stealing valuables from the deceased as a youth. But as he relates his battles with zombies, ghosts and other fiendish ghouls, his tale takes a turn for the supernatural.
Todd tries to convince a bearded lady and a living giant to join the show.
Asia attempts to swallow a sword for sword swallower's day; competition heats up among the performers.
"The Lobster Boy" joins Todd on a family trip to obtain a two-headed baby; a performer panics.
Murrugun performs a human pin cushion stunt; Creature tries to reunite with his daughter.
Todd throws a wedding; The Sadhu Hobo drops in for an unexpected visit.
Todd hosts a "Freakshow" strongman competition; a new performer's story strikes a chord.
Jesse the Half Man and Jim the Armless Wonder show off their abilities; Todd must make a difficult decision.
Todd wants to ban the word "normal"; "Freaks" travel to Venice to support the cause and hold a parade.
Soccer moms Jill and Lisa compete for approval and acceptance in a bizarre suburbia while their kids battle it out on the playing field.
Set at an institute devoted to culinary and alimentary performance, a collective finds itself embroiled in power struggles, artistic vendettas and gastrointestinal disorders.
Todd needs to find new performers for the show; a man with stretchy skin makes an appearance.
The Amazing Boobzilla performs at the show; Ali goes through surgery.
Todd brings in people from around the world for a tattoo event; Creature considers a place to live.
Asia wants to expand her electric act by adding a deadly Tesla coil stunt.
The show travels to Gibsonton, Fla., to learn about its carnival history.
Todd learns about Lobster Boy's family history; Asia searches for an apartment; George considers leaving his job.
Morgue attempts a bed of box cutters stunt; George searches for love.
The gang tries to attend a camp-out, hobo wedding for Digger and Paige; Ali and Matt have marital issues.
Creature meets his daughter face-to-face; Todd wants to throw a surprise party for Asia's 21st birthday.
Space Cowboy tries to break a world record; Danielle invites neighbors to dinner.
Zamora the Torture King tests the skeptics; Ali and Matt consider the possibility of parenthood.
Todd holds a suspension event; Phoenix starts dating.
Silvia Colloca takes a journey through regional Italy.
Once every year, passionate Italian families all over Australia answer the call of the tomato, which is considered an Italian national treasure.
Clarissa Weerase whips up some Nyonya fishcakes; Irma Mysara from Sijori Malay Eatery prepares laksa Johor; Diana shares her recipe for sweet potato churros.
Ross Magnaye shares his recipe for Filipino pork and chicken adobo; Diana whips up sinuglaw and Jacob Leung prepares a dessert called Brazo de Mercedes.
Anna shares her secrets to making flourless cookies with three different styles.
Anna bakes three different styles of crackers.
Contestants must use cheese curds in the elimination round; bakers face a wedding theme in the final showdown.
Contestants must use pineapple as an ingredient in the elimination round; the challenge of a St. Patrick's Day-themed donut showdown for the grand prize.
Jenn showcases the story behind Saskatchewan walleye and the people who bring it to the table; she visits northern Saskatchewan to learn how to catch, clean and cook walleye.
From fresh milk on the farm to raw milk cheese and handcrafted ice cream, Jenn experiences it all while learning about milk's many uses.

Chuck visits Nutashkuan, where he learns how to go lobster fishing the traditional Innu way; during his visit, he meets Edouard Kaltush, who proudly shows him how to make an artisanal harpoon and how to cook bannock under the sand.

Chuck travels to Mistissini, where an extraordinary fishing experience awaits him on the largest natural lake in Quebec; he meets Conrad Mianscum, Mistissini's tourism planner, who tells him all about this growing community of close to 4,000 people.
Jamie cooks up his tikka chicken, a very quick roast; making a vibrant carrot and grain salad and speedy crab spaghetti; for dessert, Jamie makes chocolate orange shortbread.
Stress-free sausage carbonara; spicy one-pot Thai red chicken soup; scrambled egg omelette; steamed puddings with sticky marmalade glaze.
On the menu this time is chicken dim sum, coconut buns, cucumber pickle and hoisin sauce; crackin' crab briks, couscous salad and salsa.
Jamie cooks crispy duck and hoisin lettuce parcels, chicken cacciatore, and spaghetti and smoky tomato sauce.

Raymond Blanc shares his favorite French classics, from his Maman Blanc's steak and red wine jus, to a heritage salad with mozzarella as well as tomatoes straight from his gardens; Jean-Christophe Novelli cooks a delicious mouclade des boucholeurs.
A Golden Ticket to the final is on the line as the cooks prepare an elaborate high tea and turn up the heat in a bubbling Zumbo Test.
The home cooks build towering structures and complete a terrifyingly tiny Zumbo Test, with the winner going to the final.
The finalists face a Zumbo Test before the final Sweet Sensations task -- a fairy tale-inspired showstopper.
When crowd-pleasing tacos fall apart, a cook's future is on the line; Michele Forgione's fridge is opened up to reveal 'Nduja.'

Gordon ends his Indian food adventure by travelling south to Kerala for the ultimate seafood curry. Later, in Tamil Nadu, he tries bullock racing and also faces his biggest culinary nightmare: living in an ashram where the only food on the menu is vegetarian. The last stop finds Gordon in Mumbai where he samples street food in Asia's largest slum and, later, cooks alongside one of India's top chefs, Hemant Oberoi.

Gordon heads off the tourist track into impenetrable north-east India, home of the country's best-kept culinary secrets. Leaving the 21st-century behind, he immerses himself in the life of a local meat-loving tribe in Nagaland, visits Assam to enter a housewives' competition, and finally heads off to Calcutta where he sets up shop among the street food stalls hoping to tempt the local foodies into buying his curry.
Tattoo Fixers meet Will, who needs Lou's help covering a famous face in an intimate place. Jay is assisting glamour model Gigi, who has the initials of not one, but two exes on her breast.

New addition to the tattoo parlour, Alice, covers a cringe-worthy celebrity crush for booty-shaking Abby, stubborn Jordan needs to lose the ink he got to win an argument, and Sketch has to tackle Adam's rather personal tatt.

The parlour gets a visit from Stephen, who now, as a respectable dad, wants to give the finger to a very crude tattoo he had done 20 years ago. Alice welcomes Rob, a tattoo-mad ex-solider whose mum thinks his phallic self-portrait is a step too far.

Steve, survivor of a horrific house fire, wants to cover his scarring with a special Celtic knot design. Danny, whose portrait of Tupac ended in disaster, is helped out by both Sketch and Jay as he gets a brand-new portrait of the late rapper.

For the last 18 months ex Michelin-starred chef Nick has owned and run Rococo, but his past success is now eluding him. The menu is past its sell-by date, the service is stuffy, the food is over-priced and the only thing being fed is his ego. With debts of £100k, Gordon forces him to face his failures, strips down the menu and dismantles the claustrophobic dining room.

Gordon Ramsay is back with his trademark mix of tough talking and inspirational leadership for another foray into some of the country's scariest kitchens. The venue is Ruby Tate's in Brighton, owned and run by ex-actor and failed Hollywood wannabe Allan Love. It's an oyster bar and seafood restaurant, but Allan's never tasted the food because he hates fish. Can Gordon persuade Allan to shape up?

Gordon takes on The Priory, a 100-seater carvery in Haywards Heath, Sussex. It's owned by ex-IT consultant Scott and located in a beautiful former convent, offering bargain roast dinners. Scott bought the place for £300,000, but with an ageing clientele eating for half price, he's losing £5,000 a week. Despite the heavenly location, the food is straight from hell.

Piccolo Teatro is a bijou vegetarian restaurant in Paris run by feisty Scot Rachel. A former waitress at the restaurant, Rachel bought it three years ago and now, along with best friend Stephanie, she's trying to convert the carnivorous French into a nation of veggies. For Gordon, his trip to Piccolo Teatro turns into one of his biggest nightmares yet. Will he be able to perform a miracle, or admit defeat?

It's Tim and Amelia's turn to host the rival B&B owners at their non-star-rated boutique accommodation, Nearwater, on the south Cornish coast. After a detailed inspection from Mike and Danny, they find fuel for their fire in some rather surprising places. Eva's feeling confident about a good night's sleep after testing the mattress, and Sylvie and Alan are still trying to get their head around what 'boutique' really means.

Alan and Sylvie are first to host in their seafront establishment Watersedge Guest House in Barton on Sea, Hampshire. The first guests to arrive are Blackpool boys Mike and Danny of Homecliffe Hotel, who locate dust and grime enough to grumble. Next through the door are Tim and Amelia, owners of Nearwater B&B, St Mawes. Austrian-born Eva of the Roundhouse Hotel in Weymouth, loves her spacious garden room.

Showmen Mike and Danny host their rival B&B owners on day four at their four-star rated guest house - Homecliffe Hotel - in Blackpool. After the harsh criticism Tim and Amelia received from Mike and Danny, the couple arrive at Homecliffe determined to find problems with the cleanliness of the room.

It's the turn of Austrian-born Eva Buschmann to host in her cosmopolitan boutique B&B on the Weymouth seafront, the Roundhouse Hotel. First to arrive are Danny and Mike who are a little shocked when Eva offers them a double room with an exposed shower.
It's the final day and the B&B hosts gather for one last time to find out how much they've been paid. Unfortunately, some of the hosts find their emotions running away with them.

Robertsbrooke Guesthouse in Swanage is run by Claire Hilton, who feels she has got more than a sporting chance in the competition. However, her first guests Lynn Self and Ziggy Broome are dubious about the cleanliness of their bedroom.

Quirky couple Lynn Self and Ziggy Broome hope to impress with their two-star paradise Eden Lodge in Falmouth, Cornwall. However, with two of the guests - Charlotte Church's parents James and Maria Church - already saying that they wouldn't stay anywhere below a four star, it could be an interesting day. From the offset the guests are wildly unimpressed by their surroundings, from peeling wallpaper to a dirty toilet brush.

Dexby Townhouse in Cardiff is run by Charlotte Church's parents, James and Maria. The hosts lay on a day of white-water rafting in tight wetsuits and some magic tricks courtesy of Maria's young nephew Elliot. However, the next morning some of the guests are kept waiting for their breakfast.

It is the last stay of the competition and the turn of newlyweds Pip Easby and Nicky Lesser-Easby, who run Muddifords Court Country House in Devon. The Churches find their historical four-poster bed a bit small, while not all the guests enjoy the trip to a local glassblowing factory. Over dinner some of the participants say what they think of each other, and during the night James gets cold feet.

The group meet one last time to find out exactly how much they have been paid by their fellow hoteliers, and to air their grievances face to face. Claire suspects a disappointing payment from James and Maria Church, but an underpayment from a surprising source soon changes the group dynamics. As the final hosts Pip and Nicky prepare to open their envelope, it is still anyone's guess as to who will take the title.

The Tattoo Fixers need to rescue more than just skin. They also have the challenge of saving a wedding, as Sam's embarrassing tattoo has earned him a serious ultimatum. Elsewhere, the team tackle some holiday ink that Ryan doesn't remember getting.
Sonic conquers a vehicle designed to locate and destroy living tissue matter during a solo mission to the Badlands.
Sonic defeats Robotnik's vehicle, which is designed to locate living tissue, during a mission to the Badlands; when Sonic returns, the Freedom Fighters hold a social gathering for him.
When Sally uncovers Robotnik's plan to seed the clouds with toxic rain, they attempt a mission to sabotage it.
Robotnik makes an announcement that he and Queen Aleena will be wed so he can become king of Mobius.
A captain of the Queen's guard is captured before he can reach the secret rendezvous where he was to meet Queen Aleena.
A homecoming is interrupted for Sonic, Sonia and Manic when Sleet and Dingo arrive to collect back taxes after returning to their birthplace.
Sonia discovers that the watch she received from her friend is actually a monitoring device for the Robotnik Intelligence Agency.
Sleet and Dingo plan to collect the taxes owed to Robotnik from the Duke of Velcronia but keep it for themselves.
Robotnik blackmails Cyrus by kidnapping his father and holding him hostage.
On a trip to Port Mobius, Sonic, Manic and Sonia are told that ships are sinking due to the Mobian sea-beast.
Rumor has it that Queen Aleena's journals are buried in the city of Tashistan; Sonic and his siblings search the city for the scrolls.
While lost in the wastelands of Mobius, Sonic, Manic and Sonia stumble upon an oasis called Lake Valley Resort.

Sonic outsmarts Coconuts, then stumbles into a Convention of Bounty Hunter Robots where Robotnik puts a price on his head. After Sonic defeats all the Robot Bounty Hunters, Robotnik creates Scratch and Grounder to be his S.S.S.S.S. Squad.
Sonic and Tails head into a network of abandoned mine shafts to escape Scratch and Grounder.
Sonic saves a hedgehog girl, Breezie, from Scratch and Grounder, and falls for her; Breezie is truly a robot created by Robotnik to exterminate Sonic.

Dr. Robotnik invented a ray gun that's supposed to slow Sonic down for good; a family of sloths comes under attack from Scratch and Grounder, who use them to lure Sonic into the path of the Doc's ray.
Robotnik is in need of workers to build a huge monument of himself for Robotnik Day; he opens up the new Casino Night Zone to get gamblers to lose everything and have to work for him.
A popular cartoonist Sketch Lampoon is imprisoned in Robotnik's prison.
Warpnik escapes from the Zone of Confusion and seeks revenge.
Sonic and Tails try to help a pair of Aliens repair their ship before the Prince's baby brother destroys earth.

Robotnik's momma escapes from the home for mothers of villains and demands her birthday present! When she endangers Sonic and Tails, and they manage to have her taken back to the home, even Robotnik is glad to see her go.
Princess Sally and Antoine follow up on a lead that suggests her father, King Acorn, may be alive; Sonic attempts to rescue a captured Freedom Fighter.
Sally is taken prisoner by Robotnik and Snively, who construct a robotized Sally clone.
Sonic and the Freedom Fighters travel to Robotnik's lab hoping to decipher his Roboticizer system.
Sonic and the Freedom Fighters look for the secret scrolls that have great powers.
Sonic and Sally encounter the Guardian while on a mission to the big city to replace Nicole's malfunctioning microchip.

While on a mission to the big city to replace Nicole's malfunctioning microchip, Sonic and Sally encounter the Guardian, a mysterious cloaked figure who guards a dormant wizard named Lazar and his computer of evil spells.

Nick Smith (Cecil Kellaway), a middle-aged roadside diner owner, hires a drifter, Frank Chambers (John Garfield), to work at his restaurant. Frank quickly begins an affair with Nick's beautiful young wife, Cora (Lana Turner), and the two conspire to kill Nick and seize his assets. When they succeed, local prosecutor Kyle Sackett (Leon Ames) becomes suspicious, but is unable to build a solid case. However, the couple soon realizes that no misdeed ever goes truly unpunished.

All musically gifted race-driver Lucky Jackson (Elvis Presley) wants in Las Vegas is to score enough money for a new car motor so he can win the 🏎️ [F1] Grand Prix. When he encounters sexy swimming instructor Rusty (Ann-Margret), he considers staying around longer. After Lucky loses his winnings in the hotel pool, he's forced to remain in Vegas long enough to win back his dough -- but now he also wants to win Rusty's heart. Unfortunately, so does his slick racing enemy, Elmo (Cesare Danova).

Laurence Mackay (David Niven), a professor at Columbia University, lives happily with his wife, Kate (Doris Day), and their three children. But when he leaves his career in education to become a theater critic, his newfound celebrity causes problems with both his friends and family. A scathing review upsets a close friend, and Kate becomes jealous when his work keeps him out late feting with Broadway stars, including the particularly flirtatious Deborah Vaughn (Janis Paige).

Identical twin sisters Margaret (Bette Davis) and Edith Phillips (also Davis) haven't spoken in nearly 20 years, ever since Margaret hoodwinked the man Edith loved into marrying her instead. When Margaret's husband dies, Edith reunites with her twin -- but only to seek revenge. Killing her sister and stealing her identity, Edith has everyone convinced she's really Margaret. But when she encounters Margaret's lover, Tony (Peter Lawford), Edith uncovers a shocking secret that threatens her plans.

After filling their pockets with loot from a local bank, Frank and Ross ride toward what they hope is freedom. But the younger Buckmans, Paul (Joe Don Baker) and John (Tom Skerritt), pursue them over the rough land of the Southwest.

During World War II, Lt. Col. James H. Doolittle (Spencer Tracy) leads the U.S. Air Force in a bombing mission over Japan. Ted Lawson (Van Johnson), who has a pregnant wife at home, crash-lands in the sea off the coast of China. Stranded, Lawson must heroically endure a series of harrowing challenges to make it back home.

This classic suspense film finds New York City ad executive Roger O. Thornhill (Cary Grant) pursued by ruthless spy Phillip Vandamm (James Mason) after Thornhill is mistaken for a government agent.
